content: styrened has three separate systems touching hub/network settings: (1) core-config.yaml reticulum/config for TCP interfaces, (2) HubConnection for LXMF propagation destination tracking, (3) TUI first-run config generator with hardcoded template

The LXMF hub destination hash (6fc8bf22aa293588c9bf8d7488102e95) is hardcoded and separate from TCP transport interfaces - HubConnection.connect() uses RNS.Transport.has_path()/request_path() for LXMF store-and-forward, not for establishing TCP connections
styrened uses async-first architecture with asyncio event loop, periodic tasks for announces and cleanup
CI/CD runs on Argo Workflows on brutus K3s cluster, triggered by Argo Events GitHub webhooks. GitHub Actions removed.

Planned Network tab scope: peer list management (add/remove/edit TCPClientInterface entries), AutoInterface on/off toggle, transport mode (standalone/shared, enable_transport), all writing back to core-config.yaml and regenerating ~/.reticulum/config
get_profile_defaults() seeds config.reticulum.interfaces.peers with rns.styrene.io:4242 as a TCPClientInterface stanza
RNS TCPClientInterface peers are defined in core-config.yaml under reticulum.interfaces.peers, then generate_rns_config() writes them to ~/.reticulum/config which RNS reads at startup

CoreConfig model includes DeploymentMode enum (STANDALONE, HUB, etc.), PeerConfig (host, port, name), ServerInterfaceConfig (enabled, listen_ip, port), and InterfaceConfig (peers list, auto bool, server) under config.reticulum.interfaces

Settings screen Network tab redesign is in progress: removing hub selector/KNOWN_HUBS/STYRENE_HUB_ADDRESS UI, replacing with TCPClientInterface peer manager (add/remove/edit), AutoInterface toggle, transport mode (DeploymentMode enum), and server interface config. Save writes both core-config.yaml and regenerates ~/.reticulum/config.
Config serialization uses _serialize_config() which converts CoreConfig to dict; PeerConfig entries without a name omit the name key from serialized output
Config validation via validate_core_config() returns errors with field names — validates peer host non-empty, port in valid range, and hub mode requiring server or peer interfaces
Settings save now persists network config to both core-config.yaml (via save_core_config) AND regenerates ~/.reticulum/config (via generate_rns_config + write_text) so RNS picks up changes on restart
KNOWN_HUBS dict, hub_select widget, custom hub address input, and hub announce interval have been removed from the settings screen - replaced by the interface manager panels

Settings screen Network tab now has 5 panels: TRANSPORT (mode, enable_transport, announce_interval), PEERS (dynamic add/remove TCPClientInterface rows), LOCAL DISCOVERY (AutoInterface toggle), SERVER (TCPServerInterface enable/IP/port), BATMAN-ADV MESH (existing mesh settings)

The LXMF hub address, hub selector (KNOWN_HUBS), and hub_announce_interval fields have been removed from the TUI settings screen as part of the Network tab redesign. Hub/propagation is handled separately from the interface manager.
Peer list in Network tab now has column headers (Name/Host/Port) rendered as a .peer-header-row of Static widgets with .peer-header CSS class above the dynamic peer rows

styrene --upgrade CLI runs pipx upgrade styrene (or pip install --upgrade) then pkill -f styrened daemon. styrene --reset backs up configs as .bak, regenerates core-config.yaml and ~/.reticulum/config from defaults, and kills daemon.

TUI app's _show_upgrade_screen callback calls _restart_tui() which uses os.execvp to re-exec the process. _restart_tui() finds the styrene entry point (argv0 or shutil.which), calls self.exit(), then registers atexit handler to exec after Textual teardown.

UpgradeScreen upgrade flow: _build_upgrade_cmd() detects pipx vs pip and uses --upgrade-strategy=eager to force transitive dep upgrades. _do_upgrade() runs subprocess in @work thread with 120s timeout, streams output to Log widget, then kills daemon via pkill. Dismiss returns bool to app callback.

Settings screen tab navigation uses [ and ] screen-level keyboard bindings that delegate to TabbedContent.action_previous/next_tab, bypassing arrow key consumption by Input widgets inside tab panes (v0.10.46)

UpgradeScreen._build_upgrade_cmd() passes --upgrade-strategy=eager for both pipx and pip paths. For pipx, uses '--pip-args=--upgrade-strategy=eager' as single combined argument (fixed from two separate args that pipx couldn't parse).

RNS interfaces have .online attribute for connection status, accessible via RNS.Transport.interfaces — rns_service._log_interface_status() and _last_interface_states dict track UP/DOWN state changes at runtime

TUI has 19+ files with inline CSS (CSS = or DEFAULT_CSS =): screens (upgrade, contacts, conversation, exploration, inbox, provision, confirm_flash, mesh_device_detail) and widgets (chat_widget, config_form, activity_feed, node_info_panel, hardware_panel, message_bubble, image_preview, uptime_panel, highlighted_panel, page_browser, forge_log). Main theme CSS lives in imperial_crt.tcss.

Textual ColorSystem has limited built-in theme variables (primary, secondary, warning, error, success, accent, foreground, background, surface, panel, boost, text_alpha). Custom variables are added via the 'variables' dict parameter. styrene_brand.py adds: border, border-blurred, block-cursor-*, footer-*, input-*, scrollbar*, and text-muted.

Settings screen uses Switch (not Checkbox) for all toggles as of v0.10.52. Switch renders as a sliding toggle. CSS class .setting-checkbox styles it borderless/transparent/compact. Save handler queries Switch widgets, not Checkbox. Tests use Switch import.

Custom Textual theme variable $text-muted added to styrene_brand.py ColorSystem variables dict, mapped to STYRENE_DARK['muted_foreground'] (#9ca3af) — provides readable muted text color for descriptions and headers. Used in imperial_crt.tcss for .setting-description and .peer-header.

TUI scrollbar architecture (v0.10.54): Screen-level global scrollbar rules (scrollbar-background:$surface, scrollbar-color:$border, size:1). Blanket transparent background rule for VerticalScroll/ScrollableContainer/RichLog/Log/TextArea. Individual widgets (ActivityFeed, ForgeLog, ChatWidget) have explicit scrollbar styling in DEFAULT_CSS. All scrollable containers must set background+scrollbar-track+scrollbar-thumb.

styrene-pypi sync-version.yml now builds and publishes to PyPI directly (not via release event cascade). GITHUB_TOKEN-created releases cannot trigger other workflows (GitHub anti-cascade). The workflow: detect new styrened on PyPI → bump pyproject.toml → commit+tag → build wheel → publish to PyPI → create GitHub release. Cron hourly + repository_dispatch from Argo.
Local PyPI publish path added: justfile 'publish' recipe runs .venv/bin/python -m build + .venv/bin/python -m twine upload dist/* for immediate availability instead of waiting for Argo CI

Argo release-build.yaml uses twine upload --skip-existing, so local pre-publishing via 'just publish' doesn't break the Argo pipeline — it silently skips the already-uploaded wheel and continues to OCI build and GitHub Release steps

RNS announce callback chain is being investigated to determine if the receiving interface name is available in announce handlers — needed for correlating discovered devices to their source hub/peer for hierarchical display

RNS.Transport dispatches announce handlers via inspect.signature() parameter count detection (3, 4, or 5 params) and runs each handler in a separate daemon thread via threading.Thread(target=job, daemon=True).start()

RNS announce handler callback signature is fixed at 3-5 params (destination_hash, announced_identity, app_data, announce_packet_hash, is_path_response) — receiving interface is NOT passed to handlers. However, RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5] stores the receiving_interface object post-announce, with .name attribute matching config stanza name.

NodeStore SQLite schema uses ALTER TABLE migrations for new columns (try/except OperationalError pattern) — lxmf_destination_hash, short_name, system_fingerprint were added this way. Same pattern will be used for discovered_via column.

Hierarchical mesh device tree implemented in dashboard — MeshDeviceTree(Tree) widget replaces flat DataTable, grouping discovered devices under their source interface (e.g., 'Styrene Community Hub' branch → child devices, 'Direct / Unknown' → devices without interface info). Uses MeshDevice.discovered_via field populated from RNS.Transport.path_table[dest_hash][5].name post-announce.

NodeStore 'nodes' table has discovered_via TEXT column (ALTER TABLE migration pattern) with idx_discovered_via index. UPSERT uses COALESCE(excluded.discovered_via, nodes.discovered_via) to preserve existing interface info when new announce lacks it.

MeshDevice.discovered_via field populated in StyreneAnnounceHandler.received_announce() by looking up RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5].name — index 5 is the receiving interface object with a .name attribute matching the config stanza name.

NodeStore has 'paths' table with interface_type and interface_name columns per destination_hash. The 'nodes' table now has a discovered_via TEXT column (added via ALTER TABLE migration) with idx_discovered_via index for efficient dashboard Tree grouping. UPSERT uses COALESCE to preserve existing interface info.

DashboardScreen event handling changed from on_data_table_row_selected(DataTable.RowSelected) to on_tree_node_selected(Tree.NodeSelected[str]) for device detail navigation. Tree node .data carries device identity string; None data on branch/empty nodes is ignored.

NodeInfoPanel renders in two-column layout as of v0.10.61. Left column: SYSTEM (CPU/RAM/NET/STORAGE), DAEMON (IPC mode only), IDENTITY (name/alias/hash/PQC tier). Right column: RETICULUM (RNS status/uplink/interfaces), STYRENE (mode/hub/mesh count), VERSION (styrened __version__). Uses Rich markup with regex-based padding for side-by-side rendering within a single Static widget. render() delegates to _render_left_column() and _render_right_column() methods. Located at src/styrened/tui/widgets/node_info_panel.py.

HighlightedPanel (Vertical) composes: hp-top Static (1 line) + hp-content Vertical + hp-bottom Static (1 line). hp-content default is height:auto (safe for modals/settings). Dashboard panels (#mesh-devices-panel, #activity-feed-panel) override hp-content to height:1fr via CSS specificity. Box-drawing borders rendered via Rich markup with ColorCascade hex colors.
styrened TUI uses Textual 8.0.0 as of 2026-03-01

Two identity systems coexist: (1) RNS operator identity — cryptographic keypair at reticulum.operator_identity_path, identity hash for routing, (2) Styrene IdentityConfig — display_name, icon, short_name for human-readable appearance. Both stored in core-config.yaml under different sections (reticulum vs identity). Investigation ongoing to ensure they don't conflict.

YubiKey identity provider uses FIDO2 hmac-secret extension to derive deterministic 64-byte RNS identity (X25519 + Ed25519) from hardware token. Two application-specific salts (styrene-encryption-v1, styrene-signing-v1) produce independent 32-byte outputs via getAssertion. Credential ID stored in config as base64. Located at src/styrened/services/yubikey.py. Requires pip install styrened[yubikey] (python-fido2>=1.0).

Identity provider selection in _resolve_identity_path(): priority 0 is YubiKey (if identity_config.provider == 'yubikey'), then config override path, system /etc/styrene/identity, user ~/.config/styrene/identity, LXMF app detection, and finally new generation. YubiKey path calls derive_identity_bytes() and RNS.Identity.from_bytes() inline, returning hex hash directly without writing to disk.

get_operator_identity() and get_operator_identity_object() now delegate to _load_identity_config() which loads IdentityConfig from core-config.yaml, then check provider field. YubiKey provider calls derive_identity_bytes() inline; file provider falls through to _resolve_identity_path() + from_file(). get_operator_identity() wraps get_operator_identity_object() with hash extraction and exception handling.

Well-known RNS community hubs include: dublin.connect.reticulum.network:4965 (Dublin Hub), reticulum.betweentheborders.com:4242 (BetweenTheBorders), istanbul.reserve.network:9034, node01.rns.bnz.se:4242, rns.stoppedcold.com:4242, rtclm.de:4242, sydney.reticulum.au:4242. These are being added alongside rns.styrene.io:4242 as default/selectable peer interfaces.

TUI peer rows replaced static status indicator (● dot with CSS color classes) with a Switch toggle (peer_enabled_{i}) that controls the PeerConfig.enabled field. Switch uses .setting-checkbox and .peer-enabled-toggle CSS classes. Peer enabled state persists to core-config.yaml and controls whether the peer is written to ~/.reticulum/config.

PeerConfig model now has an 'enabled' field (default True) — parsed from core-config.yaml via _parse_bool(p.get('enabled', True)), serialized as 'enabled' key in _serialize_config(), and used by generate_rns_config() to skip disabled peers (continue if not peer.enabled).

WELL_KNOWN_HUBS constant defined in models/config.py — list of 5 PeerConfig entries (Styrene Community Hub enabled, 4 community hubs disabled by default). Used by both daemon (services/config.py) and TUI (tui/services/config.py) config generators to seed new installs.

Config loaders (daemon services/config.py and TUI tui/services/config.py) merge missing WELL_KNOWN_HUBS as disabled entries after parsing peers list. Keyed by (host, port) tuple to avoid duplicates. Existing peers are never modified — only missing hubs are appended with enabled=False. This ensures existing installs see well-known hubs in Settings without manual addition.

MeshDeviceTree CSS changed in latest fix: .tree--cursor background changed from $surface to $background (eliminates visible gray shadow bar on selected row), .tree--highlight changed from $background to transparent (hover no longer shows background change). Selected row identified by $primary color + bold text only.

StyreneConfig.identity is a property that proxies to StyreneConfig.core.identity. The TUI load path calls _overlay_core_identity() which reads core config via load_core_config() and replaces config.core.identity with the loaded IdentityConfig. Settings screen Input widgets are populated from self.config.identity.display_name at compose() time.
No image/media handling exists in StyreneEnvelope wire protocol yet — image attachment support is greenfield. No content_type, attachment, or media fields in models/styrene_wire.py or protocols/.

Wire protocol image attachment design for StyreneEnvelope: MediaAttachment struct with content_type, data, original_type (for lossless JPEG repack tracking), thumbnail (progressive prefix), width, height. Defined in docs/image-format-assessment.md in styrene-rs repo. Vec<MediaAttachment> on envelope.

Image attachment design for StyreneEnvelope finalized: MediaAttachment(content_type, data, original_type, thumbnail, width, height). JXL as native format with JPEG fallback. original_type tracks lossless JPEG repacks for reversible extraction. Target 15-50KB per image. Progressive decode for mesh UX (2KB→1/8 res, 10KB→1/4 res, full). Design doc at styrene-rs/docs/image-format-assessment.md.

JXL Rust crate ecosystem (2026-03): jxl-oxide 0.12 (pure Rust decoder, active, modular sub-crates), zune-jpegxl 0.5 (pure Rust encoder, early), jxl-encoder 0.1 (pure Rust, early), jpegxl-rs 0.13 (libjxl C bindings). For styrene-mesh, jxl-oxide is primary decode, jpegxl-rs or zune-jpegxl for encode (TBD evaluation).

Python-Rust binding landscape: PyO3 (v0.23+, production-grade, standard choice — used by Polars, ruff, Pydantic V2) + Maturin (v1.8+, build backend for PyO3→wheels) is the clear winner. Also: pyo3-asyncio (Rust futures↔asyncio), rust-numpy (zero-copy ndarray), uniffi (Mozilla multi-lang IDL). Potential future use: styrene-imagecodecs PyO3 crate wrapping jxl-oxide to eliminate libjxl system dep for Python.

JXL lossless JPEG repack flow for Styrene: phone sends JPEG → Styrene wraps to JXL losslessly (20% smaller) with original_type='image/jpeg' → transmit over mesh → receiver can decode JXL or extract bit-exact original JPEG for non-Styrene clients. Zero quality loss, reversible.

Incremental Rust migration strategy via PyO3 FFI proposed in styrene-rs/docs/incremental-rust-migration.md. Two integration modes: (1) wire interop (independent Rust daemon over LXMF), (2) FFI hybrid (Rust modules exposed via PyO3 as styrene-native package, imported by Python daemon as drop-in replacements). Uses try/except ImportError pattern for graceful fallback to pure Python.

styrene-native PyO3 crate planned at crates/bindings/styrene-native/ — cdylib extension module built with maturin, re-exports from styrene-mesh/styrene-rns/styrene-lxmf crates. Installed via pip install styrened[native]. Falls back to pure Python when not installed.

styrene-rs PARITY_GAPS.md shows ~37K Rust LOC across 6 crates with 212 tests. Missing service layer (~12K LOC): conversation service, auto-reply, node store persistence, remote terminal, protocol registry, file transfer, hub connection. Critical gaps: IFAC multi-hop bug, Serial/KISS interface, propagation store-and-forward, config system.

Dual-path compatibility verification strategy: pytest fixture with params=['python','rust'] runs every test twice against both implementations. Any behavioral divergence caught immediately. Impossible with wire-only approach. Feature flag STYRENE_NATIVE=0 forces pure Python in production.

styrene-rs has two integration modes with styrened: (1) Wire interop — independent Rust daemon communicates over LXMF mesh (styrened-rs binary), (2) FFI hybrid — Rust modules exposed via PyO3 (styrene-native package) imported by Python daemon as drop-in replacements. Wire protocol (StyreneEnvelope in styrene-mesh crate) remains the shared contract for mode 1. Mode 2 enables incremental migration.

styrene-native PyO3 crate scaffolded at crates/bindings/styrene-native/ in styrene-rs repo. Cargo.toml defines cdylib crate type with pyo3 0.23 + extension-module feature, depending on styrene-mesh and styrene-rns path deps. pyproject.toml uses maturin>=1.0 build backend. Package name: styrene-native, lib name: styrene_native.

styrene-mesh crate's wire protocol uses StyreneMessage struct (not StyreneEnvelope) with encode()/decode() methods. Wire format: 10-byte namespace 'styrene.io' + 1-byte version (0x01) + 1-byte type enum + 16-byte request_id + variable msgpack payload. Header is 28 bytes. StyreneMessageType enum covers Control, Status, RPC Commands/Responses, Terminal Sessions, and PQC Sessions ranges.

Python styrened service layer LOC breakdown: reticulum.py 1407, conversation_service.py 1316, lxmf_service.py 1114, config.py 1075, node_store.py 986, doctor.py 753, rns_service.py 653, file_transfer.py 637, auto_reply.py 634, page_browser.py 524, hardware.py 518, pqc_session.py 424, attachment_store.py 359, hub_connection.py 342. Total services ~12.5K LOC. Models total ~17K LOC (styrene_wire.py alone is 1124).

StyreneApp.action_interrupt() implements double ctrl+c quit pattern: single ctrl+c pops screen stack toward dashboard, second ctrl+c within 1.0s window exits app. Uses time.monotonic() tracking via _last_interrupt class var. Binding uses priority=True to bypass focused widget key consumption.

LXMF propagation destination populated in TUI settings from config.core.lxmf.propagation_destination. Community Hub Switch toggle (#community_hub_enabled) auto-fills propagation_destination Input with COMMUNITY_HUB_PROPAGATION_HASH on enable, clears on disable (only if it matches the community hash). Empty propagation field despite enabled hub suggests config.core.lxmf.propagation_destination is None/empty at load time.

TUI config loading changed from _overlay_core_identity() (identity-only) to _overlay_core_config() which replaces entire config.core with load_core_config() result. This means core-config.yaml is the single source of truth for ALL CoreConfig fields (identity, reticulum, lxmf, rpc, discovery, api). tui.yaml still contains a stale copy of reticulum/rpc/etc sections that gets parsed then overwritten by the overlay.

_overlay_core_config() in tui/services/config.py replaces entire config.core with load_core_config() result. core-config.yaml is the single source of truth for all CoreConfig fields. Identity is stored in core-config.yaml, settings screen _save_identity() writes there first, then updates self.config.core.identity in memory so subsequent save_core_config() preserves new values.

MeshDeviceTree does NOT filter LOST nodes — all device statuses (ACTIVE, STALE, LOST) are displayed with different status symbols (● active, ◐ stale, ○ lost). Previous DataTable implementation filtered LOST nodes out.

_deduplicate_by_identity() in services/reticulum.py both deduplicates by identity_hash AND filters out devices with last_announce older than 30 minutes (cutoff = now - 1800). LOST devices are not filtered by status — they're filtered by age. Devices <30min old with LOST status still appear in the tree.

_parse_config_dict in tui/services/config.py now parses 'identity' and 'lxmf' sections from config.yaml/tui.yaml in addition to tui/fleet/provisioning/mesh/reticulum/rpc sections. Identity parsed only if display_name is non-empty (empty string keeps default 'Anonymous Styrene').

StyreneConfig._parse_config_dict parses: tui, fleet, provisioning, mesh, reticulum (interfaces/peers/hub), rpc, identity (display_name/icon/short_name if non-empty), and lxmf sections. Identity from config.yaml is now read but may be superseded by _overlay_core_config() if core-config.yaml has a real identity.

ContactsScreen DataTable was restructured: columns changed from ALIAS/PEER HASH/NOTES to ALIAS/STATUS/LAST MESSAGE/PEER HASH. Now cross-references IPCBridge get_devices() and get_conversations() to show live presence (● online, ◐ stale, ○ unknown) and last message preview with relative time. ContactInfo.to_dict() exists on the service DTO (services/contacts.py ContactInfo dataclass), not on the SQLAlchemy Contact model (models/contacts.py).

ContactInfo (services/contacts.py) is a dataclass DTO with to_dict() and from_model() methods. Contact (models/contacts.py) is the SQLAlchemy model with no to_dict(). These are two distinct classes — ContactService returns ContactInfo instances.

DeviceInfo (ipc/messages.py) has lxmf_destination_hash and destination_hash fields. ContactsScreen presence lookup matches contact peer_hash against both device fields to find the corresponding device.

styrened.tui.menubar subpackage added at src/styrened/tui/menubar/ — macOS menu bar agent showing unread count, recent conversations, and daemon status via rumps NSApplication loop. IPC polling runs in a background asyncio thread. Architecture: rumps event loop on main thread, asyncio IPC loop in daemon thread, shared state via MenuBarState dataclass with threading.Lock.
MenuBar agent uses osascript for native macOS notifications (display notification command via subprocess.Popen) rather than pyobjc or native APIs — lightweight, no additional deps.
ChatWidget._pending_attachment dict tracks staged attachments with keys: awaiting_path (bool), data_b64, filename, mime. Attachment sent on next message submission.
rumps added to pyproject.toml [tui] extras with sys_platform='darwin' marker. Import in agent.py still has friendly ImportError message as fallback.

ChatWidget on_paste() handler detects clipboard image data (screenshots via NSPasteboardTypePNG/TIFF) before falling back to file path text. Calls _stage_from_clipboard() for image data, _stage_attachment_from_path() for path text. Supported path file types expanded beyond images to include pdf, txt, md, zip, tar, gz, mp3, wav, ogg, mp4, mov.

Clipboard integration module added at src/styrened/tui/menubar/clipboard.py — reads image data and file references from macOS clipboard using PyObjC AppKit. Priority: PNG image data → TIFF image data → file URL references (Finder copy) → text that looks like a file path. Returns ClipboardAttachment dataclass with data_b64, filename, mime, size, source fields.

action_attach_file (a key) now tries clipboard first via read_clipboard_attachment() before prompting for a file path. action_paste_attachment (ctrl+v binding) explicitly stages clipboard content when widget is focused in message-browsing mode.
pyobjc-core and pyobjc-framework-Cocoa 12.1 are already available in the styrened venv (pulled in by rumps dependency) — AppKit imports work without adding new deps.

_stage_from_clipboard() async worker reads clipboard in executor, sets _pending_attachment dict, displays status with source label (📋 screenshot, 📋 copied image, 📎 file, 📎 path), and focuses chat input for optional message text.

ChatWidget action_attach_clipboard() calls _attach_from_clipboard_or_prompt() via run_worker — if clipboard read returns None, falls back to path prompt by setting awaiting_path:True and focusing the Input. Worker errors are not explicitly caught in on_worker_state_changed.

NodeInfoPanel reactive vars for comms/traffic: unread_count, conversation_count, contact_count, messages_sent, messages_received, pending_deliveries, auto_reply_enabled, propagation_enabled, transport_enabled, active_links. _load_comms_data() populates from local SQLite DB in standalone mode; IPC bridge populates in daemon mode.
Dashboard panel CSS proportions (v0.12.0): #node-info-panel height:auto max-height:28, #mesh-devices-panel height:2fr min-height:6, #activity-feed-panel height:1fr min-height:4 max-height:16.

NodeInfoPanel _render_left_column() has sections: SYSTEM, COMMS (inbox unread, chats count, contacts count, auto-reply status), IDENTITY; _render_right_column() has sections: RETICULUM, STYRENE, TRAFFIC (msg sent/recv, pending, active links, transport/propagation roles), VERSION
Exploration table has HOPS and VIA columns as of v0.12.1. HOPS from RNS.Transport.path_table[dest][2], VIA from discovered_via. Both sortable. MeshDevice model extended with optional hops field.

ChatWidget._last_displayed_date tracks the most recent date separator rendered, enabling date separator continuity across incremental message appends. _maybe_mount_date_separator() helper mounts a separator Static when the message date changes.

ChatWidget message format (v0.13.0): outgoing uses 'content icon HH:MM' right-padded (8-char left margin), incoming uses sender name on own line + 'content HH:MM' left-padded (8-char right margin). No 'ME:' prefix on outgoing. Position, color, and alignment differentiate sender.

RNS.Transport.path_table keys are bytes (raw destination hash bytes), not hex strings. Index 5 is receiving_interface object. This matches the existing implementation in StyreneAnnounceHandler which passes bytes destination_hash to path_table.get().

RNS.Transport.path_table entry index 1 (received_from) contains the next-hop transport node hash that relayed the announce — distinct from index 5 (interface) which is the local interface. Both are available for richer VIA display.

ExplorationScreen has a fifth 'Styrene' tab (tab-styrene) added before the existing 4 tabs, using StyreneFleetTable (DataTable subclass) instead of ReticumAnnounceTable, with columns NAME/VERSION/CAPABILITIES/HOPS/VIA/STATUS/LAST ANNOUNCE and Styrene-specific filtering/deduplication via _deduplicate_by_identity().

ExplorationScreen has five tabs (Styrene, LXMF, Pages, Infrastructure, Other). _EXPLORATION_TYPES excludes DeviceType.STYRENE_NODE from generic discovery. Styrene tab uses StyreneFleetTable with fleet-specific columns. ReticumAnnounceTable is shared by the other 4 tabs. _STYRENE_TYPES = frozenset({DeviceType.STYRENE_NODE}).

StyreneFleetTable (DataTable[str]) at exploration.py shows Styrene fleet nodes with columns NAME, VERSION, CAPABILITIES, HOPS, VIA, STATUS, LAST ANNOUNCE. Capability icons: 📨 autoreply, ⚡ exec, 🔌 rpc, 🔀 transport. Deduplicates via _deduplicate_by_identity(). Sortable by all columns. Has set_filter(), sort_by(), refresh_data() methods. Standalone mode reads from node_store.get_styrene_nodes() + discover_devices().

IPC CMD_RETRY_MESSAGE handler fully implemented in handlers.py: prepare_retry() → reset to PENDING → rebuild LXMF payload → send via lxmf_service.send_message() with delivery callbacks → register_delivery_tracking() → mark_sent(). Returns ErrorResponse.not_found if message not in FAILED state.

_resolve_identity() Strategy 5 implemented: requests RNS path + parallel identity_hash path request, then polls for up to 10s (0.5s sleep intervals) for identity to arrive via re-announce or path response. IPC handlers wrap send_message calls in run_in_executor to prevent event loop blocking during the 10s wait.

lxmf_service.send_message() returns None when: (1) LXMF not initialized, (2) _resolve_identity() returns None after exhausting 5 strategies: direct RNS recall, NodeStore operator dest lookup, NodeStore LXMF dest lookup, persistent storage load, Strategy 5 (request_path + 10s poll loop). Strategy 5 blocks calling thread up to 10s — IPC handlers call send_message via run_in_executor to isolate blocking. send timeout bumped to 30s in TUI.

MeshDeviceDetailScreen._resolve_nomadnet_destination() checks if the device is a NOMADNET_NODE directly, or queries NodeStore for any node with matching identity_hash and DeviceType.NOMADNET_NODE — enabling Pages tab for Styrene nodes that co-announce NomadNet aspects (same RNS identity, different destination hash).

NomadNet pages are a feature set of a Styrene node: same RNS identity produces separate destination hashes for different announce aspects — ('nomadnetwork','node') for NomadNet pages and ('styrene_node','operator') for Styrene. Devices sharing an identity_hash are the same physical node.
NomadNet pages use Micron (.mu) format, stored at ~/.nomadnetwork/storage/pages/. Demo pages live in public-hub/pages/demo/ and include index.mu, identity.mu, fleet.mu, hardware.mu etc.

_detect_hardware() in page_server.py reads hw.model via sysctl on macOS, /proc/device-tree/model on Linux SBCs (RPi), or /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name on x86. _detect_capabilities() introspects running lxmf_service, rns_service, and rpc_server singletons at page generation time.

PageServerConfig.pages_dir defaults to ~/.styrene/pages/ (None means use paths.data_dir()/pages), with enabled:false by default. PageServerService.start() creates the directory, attempts RNS destination creation, and now calls _ensure_default_index() to generate index.mu if missing.
PageServerService.regenerate_index() is a public method that overwrites index.mu with current node info — callable from TUI settings or CLI without requiring a restart.

CMD_PAGE_REGENERATE IPC command: CmdPageRegenerateRequest (no-arg), handle_cmd_page_regenerate() calls daemon._page_server_service.regenerate_index() and returns ResultResponse with {regenerated: bool, pages_dir: str|None}. Client method: IPCBridge.page_regenerate_index() returns bool.

Settings screen System tab now has a PAGES panel with: Serve Pages Switch (page_server_enabled), Node Name Input (page_server_node_name), and a 'Generate Node Page' Button (btn-generate-page), plus a description explaining the feature.

PageServerService._generate_node_info_page() includes an 'About Styrene' section with docs URL (https://docs.styrene.io), Source link (https://github.com/styrene-lab/styrened), Community Hub link, 'pipx install styrene' install hint, and rns.styrene.io:4242 connection info as mild self-promotion in the default NomadNet index page.

scripts/generate_changelog.py generates src/styrened/_changelog.py (ENTRIES list of (version, summary) tuples) from git tags at build time, embedding changelog data in the package wheel so it's available in pipx/pip installs without a git checkout.

tui/services/changelog.py: Changelog/ChangelogEntry dataclasses, fetch_changelog() with 4-strategy chain: (1) bundled _changelog.py baked at build time, (2) local git log, (3) GitHub compare API, (4) PyPI version list fallback. Strategy 1 always has commit messages and works for pipx installs. Changelog.format_lines() groups entries by version. UpgradeScreen shows WHAT'S NEW section, hides on upgrade start, runs _fetch_changelog() worker on_mount.

public-hub entrypoint-consolidated.sh runs styrened as primary process (owns RNS transport), waits for RNS storage dir, then starts NomadNet in daemon mode connecting to styrened's shared RNS instance. Hub has two monitored processes (styrened + nomadnet).

public-hub/container/Containerfile.consolidated installs styrened[web,metrics] from PyPI via ARG STYRENED_VERSION build argument, plus nomadnet==0.9.7. Demo pages from pages/demo/ are baked into the image at /app/demo-pages/ and copied to NomadNet storage/pages/ at startup by the entrypoint script.

public-hub has two Containerfiles: Containerfile (legacy — rnsd+lxmd+nomadnet, no styrened) and Containerfile.consolidated (current — styrened+nomadnet). Hub's NomadNet process owns page serving from ~/.nomadnetwork/storage/pages/, not styrened's PageServerService.

On public-hub, styrened and NomadNet are separate processes each with their own RNS identity. styrened uses ~/.styrene/identity; NomadNet uses ~/.nomadnetwork/storage/identity. These produce different identity_hashes, meaning the two announce destinations (styrene_node/operator and nomadnetwork/node) cannot be correlated by identity_hash alone.

parse_announce_data() return type extended from 7-tuple to 8-tuple by adding nomadnet_dest (str|None) as the 8th element. MeshDevice parsing now handles 8-field announce format alongside legacy 4/6/7-field formats.

Styrene announce wire format extended to 8-field: 'styrene:{name}:{version}:{caps}:{lxmf_dest}:{short_name}:{fingerprint}:{nomadnet_dest}' — nomadnet_dest is the NomadNet destination hash, populated when page_server is active (edge mode: styrened owns destination; bridge mode: reads NomadNet's identity file and computes hash).

NodeStore 'nodes' table now has nomadnet_destination_hash TEXT column (ALTER TABLE migration). Saved in save_node() as 14th positional param, COALESCE preservation on UPSERT. Read back in _row_to_device() with try/except KeyError guard for older DBs.

fetch_changelog() in tui/services/changelog.py has 5-strategy chain: (1) bundled _changelog.py, (2) PyPI wheel download — fetches target version's wheel, extracts _changelog.py via zipfile, parses ENTRIES via exec, (3) local git log, (4) GitHub compare API, (5) PyPI version list fallback. Strategy 2 via _fetch_from_pypi_wheel() resolves the 'next version changelog' problem for pipx installs.

fetch_changelog() Strategy chain now has 5 strategies: (1) bundled _changelog.py (installed version), (2) download target version's wheel from PyPI and extract its _changelog.py (fixes 'what's new in NEXT version' gap for pipx installs), (3) local git log, (4) GitHub compare API, (5) PyPI version listing fallback.

_fetch_from_pypi_wheel() downloads target version's .whl from PyPI JSON API, reads the zip in-memory via zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO), extracts styrened/_changelog.py, executes it with restricted builtins, and parses ENTRIES list. Uses packaging.Version for range filtering.
NomadNet destination hash for hub's multi-process setup: af1ec9121da534836e6a39b7d261fa65 (computed from /app/.nomadnetwork/storage/identity with identity_hash 20a6dd01480cd200b46260a7e2014f88).

public-hub K8s deployment has 4 PVCs in namespace styrene-hub: lxmf-data (500Mi), nomadnet-data (500Mi), reticulum-data (100Mi), styrene-data (500Mi), all using local-path StorageClass on the brutus cluster.

page_browser.py fetch_page() flow: (1) RNS.Transport.request_path if no path, (2) poll PATH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT for path, (3) RNS.Identity.recall for identity, (4) _get_or_create_link with one retry on failure after forced path re-discovery.

NomadNet Node.py registers each page as a request handler via destination.register_request_handler('/page/<relpath>', response_generator=self.serve_page, allow=ALLOW_ALL). Executable .mu files (exec bit set) are run as scripts; non-executable are served verbatim.

PageBrowserService._get_or_create_link() creates RNS.Link to RNS.Destination(identity, OUT, SINGLE, 'nomadnetwork', 'node'), then calls link.request(path, ...) to invoke NomadNet's registered request handlers. Link establishment timeout is separate from page request timeout (step 5 asyncio.wait_for).

public-hub NomadNet pages directory has 28+ registered pages including /page/index.mu, /page/about.mu, /page/getting-started.mu, /page/connect.mu, demo/ (executable .mu scripts), and docs/ (static .mu files).

NomadNet peersettings shows served_page_requests: 3299+ and node_last_announce firing ~100s intervals — NomadNet on the hub is actively serving pages and announcing. Page browser failures are client-side link establishment issues, not a hub-side problem.

PageBrowserService can be tested standalone by initializing RNS.Reticulum() directly before creating the service — the service itself does not init RNS, it assumes it is already running (either as daemon's shared instance or caller-initialized).

rns_service._check_interface_states() debounce added: _RECONNECT_DEBOUNCE constant suppresses TCP object-identity-change reconnect events that fire within the cooldown window, preventing reconnect storms from flooding _handle_reconnection() when multiple TCP peers cycle rapidly. Uses self._last_reconnect_time class attribute.

Dividers colored dim teal (#3a6a5e). Literal blocks get │ pipe prefix. File: src/styrened/tui/widgets/micron_parser.py

PageCacheService at src/styrened/services/page_cache.py: write-through SQLite cache for NomadNet pages. Models PageCache (destination_hash+path unique, content, content_length, fetched_at) and SavedSite (destination_hash unique, display_name, refresh_interval, last_crawl_at, pages_cached, max_depth) added to models/messages.py Base. Background crawl loop refreshes saved sites at their configured interval. extract_page_links() parses micron content for same-node BFS crawling.

PageCacheService is initialized in daemon._start_page_browser() using init_db() to get the SQLAlchemy engine (not a _message_store._engine attribute), then set_page_browser() wires it to the PageBrowserService. Shutdown order: page_cache_service stopped before page_browser_service in daemon shutdown.

IPC fetch-page handler has write-through cache pattern: on status=='ok' with content, calls cache_svc.cache_page(); on non-ok status OR exception, tries get_cached_page() and returns cached_content/cached_at/cached_content_length fields in the response dict alongside the error.

PageBrowserWidget has 'S' (save_site) and 'C' (crawl_site) keybindings, and _show_cached_page() method that renders cached micron content with a ⚠ banner showing cache age and error reason when live fetch fails.

IPC cache page commands wired: CMD_PAGE_SAVE_SITE/REMOVE_SITE/LIST_SITES/CRAWL_SITE/GET_CACHED all registered in server.py dispatch table and handler methods added to handlers.py. Client methods: page_save_site(), page_remove_site(), page_list_sites(), page_crawl_site(), page_get_cached() added to client.py.

page_browser.py IPC fetch-page result now maps all error statuses (path_not_found, timeout, link_failed, not_found, error) through a single branch that checks for cached_content/cached_at fields in the result dict before showing the error, enabling offline fallback display.

extract_page_links() in page_cache.py normalizes URLs: strips colon prefix for self-references, skips cross-node links (those containing ':' after the first char), prepends '/page/' to relative paths, and appends '.mu' to extensionless path segments only when the last segment has no '.'.
PageCacheService.crawl_site() uses collections.deque for BFS queue (popleft = O(1)) as of v0.13.24. Previously used list.pop(0) which was O(n).

Planned persistent direct data link for Styrene nodes: RNS.Link established per-peer in the device detail screen, renegotiated on path change, serving as foundation for high-bandwidth direct mesh datalink system. Initialization point for future streaming status, file transfer, and real-time RPC.

Planned persistent direct data link for Styrene nodes: daemon registers RNS.Destination(identity, IN, SINGLE, 'styrene', 'datalink') to accept incoming links; DirectLinkService manages outgoing RNS.Links to peers. Link destination hash is deterministically computable from the peer's identity. Renegotiated on path change. Foundation for streaming status, file transfer, and real-time RPC multiplexing.

DeviceStatusWidget renders RPC StatusResponse in plain dashed-header sections with no cascade colors — aesthetic mismatch with Imperial CRT theme. Hub returns uptime=0, ip=127.0.0.1, services=[] (real but useless K8s container values). MeshDevice announce data (name, type, capabilities, version, hops, via, last_seen, identity) not passed to status widget; only StatusResponse RPC data is shown.

RPC server _gather_status() uses /proc/uptime (Linux), sysctl kern.boottime (macOS), socket.connect('8.8.8.8') for IP, and systemctl is-active checks for services — all fail gracefully to 0/'127.0.0.1'/[] in containers. disk usage via os.statvfs('/').

DeviceStatusWidget renders RPC data in plain dashed-header sections with no cascade colors — hub returns uptime=0 (container uptime), ip=127.0.0.1 (no route to 8.8.8.8 in K8s), services=[] (no systemctl) as real but useless values rather than the fallback sentinel.

DirectLinkService at src/styrened/services/direct_link.py manages persistent outgoing RNS.Links to Styrene peers via the ('styrene','datalink') destination aspect. Links are cached by LXMF destination hash, auto-cleaned after 5min idle, and support /status and /ping requests over the link. The daemon registers a complementary IN SINGLE destination for accepting incoming links.

RPC server at src/styrened/rpc/server_protocol.py (StyreneProtocol-based) supports PING, STATUS_REQUEST, EXEC, REBOOT, CONFIG_UPDATE, SELF_UPDATE, INBOX_QUERY, MESSAGES_QUERY. Rate limiting per identity (30 req/min), replay protection (300s window, 1000 recent IDs), authorization whitelist. Dangerous commands disabled by default.

Daemon gets self._direct_link_service and self._datalink_destination attributes added alongside existing service fields. DirectLinkService started in _start_direct_link() after page server. Reconnect handler calls direct_link_service.handle_reconnection().

_gather_status() in the RPC server now returns additional fields: styrened_version, hostname, arch, os_id, os_version, nixos_generation, available_commands — via get_os_info() from services/system_info.py.

DirectLinkService at src/styrened/services/direct_link.py integrated into daemon: daemon._direct_link_service started in _start_direct_link(), daemon._datalink_destination registers ('styrene','datalink') IN SINGLE destination with /status and /ping request handlers. _on_datalink_established() logs incoming peer links.

IPC message classes added for direct link: CmdDatalinkEstablishRequest, CmdDatalinkTeardownRequest, CmdDatalinkStatusRequest, CmdDatalinkQueryRequest — all with destination_hash field, deserialization in factory function.

IPC handler methods added for direct link: handle_cmd_datalink_establish, handle_cmd_datalink_teardown, handle_cmd_datalink_status, handle_cmd_datalink_query — all with _check_direct_link() guard checking for daemon._direct_link_service.
_serve_datalink_status() handler in daemon.py delegates to self._rpc_server._gather_status() and returns JSON bytes — direct link status response reuses RPC gather_status data.

DeviceStatusWidget rewritten as a two-column cascade-colored dashboard: left column (NODE: type/version/caps/alias, MESH: identity/dest/hops/via/nomadnet), right column (LINK: direct link status/RTT/age, SYSTEM: hostname/uptime/OS/arch/nixos/daemon version from RPC, NETWORK: IP/services/disk). IPC handlers.py gains _check_direct_link() guard and four async handler methods: handle_cmd_datalink_establish, handle_cmd_datalink_teardown, handle_cmd_datalink_status, handle_cmd_datalink_query — all use DirectLinkService.establish()/teardown()/get_link_info()/request_status().

IPC client (client.py) gains datalink_establish(), datalink_teardown(), datalink_status(), datalink_query() methods in a 'Direct data link methods' section, each calling _request() with the corresponding CmdDatalinkXxxRequest message.

IPCBridge (tui/services/ipc_bridge.py) gains datalink_establish(), datalink_teardown(), datalink_status(), datalink_query() bridge methods delegating to _call() — placed in a 'Direct data link methods' section before the subscriptions section.

DirectLinkService (v0.13.25): Persistent outgoing RNS.Links to Styrene peers via ("styrene", "datalink") destination aspect. Daemon registers IN destination with /status and /ping request handlers (JSON over link.request()). Client establishes OUT links identified by peer's LXMF dest hash, computes datalink dest hash from recalled identity. IPC: CMD_DATALINK_ESTABLISH(0x50), CMD_DATALINK_TEARDOWN(0x51), CMD_DATALINK_STATUS(0x52), CMD_DATALINK_QUERY(0x53). DirectLinkService in services/direct_link.py, daemon setup in _start_direct_link()/_setup_datalink_destination(). Idle link cleanup at 5min. Reconnect handling flags path re-discovery.

IPC CMD_DATALINK_SPEEDTEST=0x54: CmdDatalinkSpeedtestRequest(destination_hash), handle_cmd_datalink_speedtest() in handlers.py calls DirectLinkService.run_speedtest() with timeout=90.0s, returns ResultResponse({results: list}). Client method datalink_speedtest(destination_hash, timeout=120.0). IPCBridge.datalink_speedtest() bridges to _call().

MeshDeviceDetailScreen gains 'T' (run_speedtest) keybinding: checks for active link via datalink_status, runs _do_speedtest worker, displays results as notification with link RTT, per-payload throughput bar chart, and peak kbps. DeviceStatusWidget gains speedtest_results reactive that renders an ASCII bar chart in the right column.

DirectLink timeouts increased for LoRa: PATH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=45s, LINK_ESTABLISHMENT_TIMEOUT=45s, REQUEST_TIMEOUT=30s, CLEANUP_INTERVAL=120s, IDLE_LINK_TIMEOUT=900s (15min — link establishment expensive on LoRa).

DirectLinkService speedtest now RTT-adaptive: probes link.rtt, selects from PAYLOAD_SET_FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW/MINIMAL based on RTT thresholds (<200ms/<2s/<5s/>5s). Per-payload timeout auto-scales as max(30s, size*8/estimated_bps*4) or max(60s, size*8/1000*3) for LoRa. Early bail on failed transfers marks remaining sizes as 'skipped'. SPEEDTEST_DELAY_SLOW=2.0s for RTT>0.5s links.

DeviceStatusWidget gains speedtest_results reactive (list|None) that renders ASCII bar chart in right column: per-payload throughput bar (█/░ chars scaled to ~1000kbps max), peak kbps summary, failed/skipped entries in dim. Watcher calls self.refresh() when mounted.
_format_bytes(n: int) helper defined at module level in mesh_device_detail.py (after TYPE_CHECKING block) — formats int bytes as '256B', '4KB', '256MB' etc. Used in speedtest result formatting.

ReticumAnnounceTable and StyreneFleetTable both gain _hide_lost (default True), _hide_stale (default False), toggle_hide_lost()/toggle_hide_stale() methods, and status_counts property for per-status device counting. _rebuild_table() applies status filters before text filter.

Tab labels show visible/total when filtered (e.g., 'LXMF (127/1725)'). _update_status_bar() reads active table's status_counts property and hiding_lost/hiding_stale flags.

MeshDeviceDetailScreen constructor accepts optional `device: MeshDevice | None` parameter — if supplied, skips _load_device() SQLite re-query. Exploration screen now passes pre-resolved MeshDevice on navigation.

Module-level status cache in mesh_device_detail.py: _STATUS_CACHE dict keyed by identity_hash with (StatusResponse, timestamp) tuples. TTL=120s. _cache_status()/get_cached_status() helpers. Cache checked before LXMF RPC in _auto_fetch_status(), hit renders immediately without loading=True wait.

v0.13.28 released: perf: device detail screen — MeshDevice passed from exploration table (skips NodeStore re-query), StatusResponse 120s TTL cache per identity hash (_STATUS_CACHE dict), cached status renders before loading spinner in _auto_fetch_status().

CMD_TERMINAL_OPEN is dispatched via a special pre-dispatch branch in ipc/server.py (before the dispatch table lookup) because it requires the client reference for event routing. CMD_TERMINAL_INPUT/RESIZE/CLOSE are in the dispatch table. This means the 0x50-0x53 alias with datalink commands does not break terminal functionality at runtime.

IPC protocol constants for direct data link reassigned to 0x60-0x6F range to eliminate collision with terminal commands (0x50-0x5F): CMD_DATALINK_ESTABLISH=0x60, CMD_DATALINK_TEARDOWN=0x61, CMD_DATALINK_STATUS=0x62, CMD_DATALINK_QUERY=0x63, CMD_DATALINK_SPEEDTEST=0x64.

Styrene dual-layer mesh: BATMAN-ADV provides L2 physical connectivity (bat0 virtual switch over 802.11s WiFi, Ethernet, VPN), and Reticulum runs on top as an overlay using bat0 via AutoInterface. RNS.Links then provide encrypted destination-to-destination sessions over whatever transport is available. For nodes connected only via internet TCP (no local BATMAN), RNS.Links through the hub give direct encrypted channels — future work may tunnel L2 frames over these Links to extend the BATMAN domain across the internet, LoRa WAN, WiFi hotspots, and eventually LoRa radios, creating a unified IP mesh that spans all transport types.

Styrene dual-layer mesh architecture confirmed in research docs: BATMAN-ADV (bat0) is the L2 physical layer, Reticulum runs on top via AutoInterface/UDP on bat0. Existing internet TCP connections use RNS.Links through the hub for direct encrypted channels. Future work: tunnel L2 Ethernet frames over RNS.Links to extend BATMAN domain across internet, LoRa WAN, WiFi hotspots, and LoRa radios — creating a unified IP mesh spanning all transport types. See styrene/docs/src/architecture.md and styrene/research/batman-adv.md.

BATMAN-ADV over RNS overlay (future): each Styrene node gets a TAP interface managed by BATMAN-ADV, with RNS.Links serving as virtual point-to-point wires to neighbors. BATMAN-ADV then routes L2 frames across this virtual topology, giving nodes real IP addresses and arbitrary IP services (SSH, HTTP, file shares). Primary use case: extend the bat0 broadcast domain over transport types that don't support native 802.11s (internet TCP, LoRa WAN, WiFi hotspots).

batman-mesh.nix at styrene-edge/sbc/common/ implements 802.11s+BATMAN-ADV for NixOS fleet devices: NetworkManager mesh profile, batctl setup systemd service, configurable meshId/meshKey/channel/gwMode (off/client/server). bat0 is the virtual switch interface exposed to the system.

Current gap in the BATMAN↔internet bridging plan: bat0 L2 domain is local-only (WiFi/Ethernet); internet-connected nodes (TCP to hub) are in a separate L2 domain with no bat0 bridge. RNS.Links exist (DirectLinkService) but carry only Styrene overlay traffic, not raw Ethernet frames. Next step: TAP-over-RNS.Link tunnel to extend bat0 across internet/LoRa transports.
batman-adv and TAP tunneling is Linux-only — a TunnelService extending bat0 over RNS.Links cannot run on macOS (operator workstation). The L2-over-RNS tunnel feature is fleet-device-only.

macOS cannot run batman-adv because: (1) Apple's proprietary WiFi driver doesn't expose 802.11s mesh point mode, (2) batman-adv is a Linux kernel module with no XNU port, (3) Apple deprecated kexts in favor of sandboxed Network Extensions. Hardware likely supports 802.11s but Apple chose not to implement it.

Styrene mesh VPN architecture: three tiers — (1) Internet → WireGuard to mesh gateway → bat0, (2) Local WiFi → BATMAN-ADV (802.11s) → bat0, (3) LoRa-only → RNS.Link L2 tunnel → bat0. BATMAN-ADV's role is creating IP from raw radios when no infrastructure exists; WireGuard handles the internet-connected tier.
daemon.py gains self._mesh_vpn_service: Any = None alongside _direct_link_service and _datalink_destination fields.

styrened NixOS module (styrene-edge/sbc/common/styrened.nix): service user is 'styrened' (isSystemUser), group 'users'. Now includes AmbientCapabilities=['CAP_NET_ADMIN'] and CapabilityBoundingSet=['CAP_NET_ADMIN'] for WireGuard interface management. wireguard-tools added to systemPackages.

styrened.nix NixOS module: service user is 'styrened', group 'users', StateDirectory/ConfigurationDirectory 'styrened'. Now grants AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_ADMIN and CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_ADMIN for WireGuard interface management. Batman-mesh.nix adds bat0 via a separate oneshot service. wireguard-tools package added.

CoreConfig model has mesh_vpn: MeshVPNConfig field (enable, listen_port=51820, subnet_prefix='fd73:7479:7265:6e65', gateway, endpoint) in models/config.py. MeshVPNConfig defined once in models/config.py; services/mesh_vpn.py re-exports it via 'from styrened.models.config import MeshVPNConfig' for backward compatibility.

MeshVPNService at src/styrened/services/mesh_vpn.py: WireGuard tunnels bootstrapped over RNS.Link. IPv6 ULA mesh IPs (fd73:7479:7265:6e65::/64) derived as interface ID from SHA-256 of identity hash — no collisions possible at any practical scale. WG key exchange over DirectLinkService /vpn/handshake path. Platform-aware: Linux kernel WG (ip+wg), macOS userspace (wg-quick). Gateway mode bridges wg-styrene into bat0. Endpoint auto-detected via UDP socket if not configured.

MeshVPNService topology modes: 'point-to-point' (no gateway peer), 'routed' (has a gateway peer with /64 allowed-ips), 'gateway' (this node is the gateway). get_status() returns mode, has_gateway, is_gateway, subnet fields. handle_peer_lost() removes WG peer and logs degradation warning when a gateway goes offline.

Mesh subnet: RFC 4193 ULA fd73:7479:7265:6e65::/64 ('styrene' ASCII hex). Interface ID (64 bits) from SHA-256 of identity hash. derive_mesh_ip(identity_hash, subnet_prefix) returns e.g. 'fd73:7479:7265:6e65:a1b2:c3d4:e5f6:7890'. subnet_prefix in MeshVPNConfig defaults to 'fd73:7479:7265:6e65' but is configurable per-fleet. Handshake now includes subnet_prefix field to detect cross-fleet IP collisions.

WireGuard mesh VPN uses IPv6 ULA /64 subnets — macOS wg-quick config uses Address={mesh_ip}/64, Linux ip/wg uses /64. Subnet prefix exchanged in handshake payload to detect fleet isolation mismatches (peer_prefix != our_prefix returns error response with our_prefix).

build_handshake_request/response now include subnet_prefix field derived via mesh_ip.rsplit(':', 4)[0] — extracts first 4 colon-groups as the /64 prefix. parse_handshake_request/response do NOT extract or validate subnet_prefix from the payload. See src/styrened/services/mesh_vpn.py.

NodeInfoPanel col_width=44 is hardcoded, meaning the two-column layout does not adapt to the actual widget width (~136 chars at 140-col terminal). Right column always starts at char 44 regardless of available space. #node-info-panel has max-height:28 and padding:0 1.
mesh_vpn.py _create_interface_linux() uses mkstemp+fchmod(S_IRUSR|S_IWUSR)+os.write for secure private key temp file handling (not NamedTemporaryFile which creates world-readable file briefly).

MeshVPNService._on_peer_config_done(task) is a @staticmethod callback registered via task.add_done_callback() — logs task.exception() for unobserved exceptions from _configure_peer() background tasks.

mesh_vpn.py extract_prefix(mesh_ip, prefix_len=64) helper: uses ipaddress.IPv6Network(f'{mesh_ip}/{prefix_len}', strict=False).network_address.exploded to split into groups, returns ':'.join(parts[:prefix_len//16]). Replaces all rsplit-based prefix extraction.

DirectLinkService gained generic request(path, data, timeout) method; request_status() now delegates to it. Enables MeshVPNService to send /vpn/handshake via DirectLinkService.request(). See src/styrened/services/direct_link.py.

MeshVPNService BATMAN-ADV integration uses VXLAN-over-WireGuard: bat0→vxlan-<peer_prefix> (L2/UDP, per-peer)→wg-styrene (L3). _create_vxlan_for_peer()/destroy add/remove per-peer VXLAN interfaces. VXLAN_VNI=7379, dstport=4789. Only Linux/gateway mode. _vxlan_name(identity_hash)='vx-{hash[:10]}'. Old _add_to_batman/_remove_from_batman removed. See src/styrened/services/mesh_vpn.py.

mesh_vpn.py macOS root-check model: _create_interface_macos() checks os.geteuid()==0; if root uses wg-quick up automatically; if not root writes conf file and returns False with 'sudo styrened daemon' hint. _configure_peer() checks self._macos_tunnel_active before calling wg set — falls back to conf-file-only mode when not root. _macos_tunnel_active attribute set on successful wg-quick up.

mesh_vpn.py macOS privilege model: _create_interface_macos() checks os.geteuid()==0. If root: wg-quick up runs automatically (async subprocess, no sudo), all wg set peer calls work. Styrene Identity System (design node: styrene-identity, status: exploring): Root identity layer above all protocol-specific hashes. StyreneID = hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 (post-quantum signing key). Classical Ed25519 enables YubiKey-backing today; ML-DSA adds PQ forward security in software. Protocol keys (RNS, LXMF, Yggdrasil, WireGuard, I2P, SSH) are either HKDF-derived from root secret or independently generated + cross-signed via a published identity manifest. The manifest (JSON, signed) is the cross-protocol identity proof distributed via RNS/NomadNet. A resolution layer in the daemon maps ANY protocol hash to canonical StyreneID. This directly fixes the 8 TUI hash-confusion bugs: all state (contacts, conversations, unread, cache, RBAC) keyed by StyreneID. Relationship to RNS: StyreneID wraps/binds to existing RNS identity_hash (adoption, not replacement). YubiKey: Ed25519 in PIV slot; ML-DSA key encrypted on disk, unlocked via YubiKey HMAC challenge-response. Constrained nodes (RP2040/ESP32): lite mode, Ed25519 only, managed by operator's full node.

Styrene Trust Model (design node: styrene-trust-model, status: exploring, child of styrene-identity): Three trust surfaces — identity (WoT endorsements + external attestations), infrastructure (hub/node signed manifests), content (NomadNet page signatures). PGP attestation: PGP key holder signs a binding over StyreneID pubkey, travels in manifest attestations[]. Journalists/activists use existing PGP keys (WKD, keyservers) to attest their Styrene identity. WoT: peers sign each other's manifests; trust attenuates with depth (depth 1=full, depth 2=~50%, depth 3=~25%, beyond=0). Sybil resistance: attenuation model (bot farms only work if attacker compromises YOUR trusted set), attestation weight asymmetry (established PGP keys outweigh fresh StyreneIDs), rate limiting, reciprocity suspicion signals. CRITICAL: WoT influences display/discovery ONLY, never RBAC capabilities — explicit operator assignment always required for any capability grant. ABS tier (design node: styrene-abs-tier): deferred future hardened topology where PQ is mandatory and trust thresholds enforced at network level, not operator-configurable. Standard Styrene = hybrid, operator-discretion. ABS = ML-DSA mandatory, minimum endorsement requirements. Both share same RNS routing layer.

Styrene trust engine — three-layer architecture (design nodes: styrene-trust-model, styrene-distrust-model): Layer 1=Appleseed local trust (source-centric energy spreading, γ=0.5 decay, offline, per-node), Layer 2=SybilRank pre-filter (power iteration at log2|V| steps, background, gossip-assisted, produces sybil-suspicion score), Layer 3=EigenTrust global hub/content reputation (hub-computed, signed snapshots served to lite nodes via /meta). Key implementations: Rust=fluencelabs/trust-graph (cert chains), Karma3Labs/rs-eigentrust (EigenTrust, MIT), petgraph (graph substrate), privacy-ethereum/zk-eigentrust (ZK future). Python=appleseed-metric (JS reference, port to Python/Rust), Karma3Labs/openrank-sdk (EigenTrust API), thibaultlaugel/sybilguard. Privacy: endorsements encrypted-in-transit, operator-controlled, DP aggregate (ITCS 2025 framework). ZK proofs for Phase 3 (score≥threshold without revealing graph). Reference papers: Guha 2004 (empirical), Appleseed 2005, EigenTrust 2003, SybilRank 2012, Differential Privacy on Trust Graphs ITCS 2025, DeciTrustNET 2020.

Trust engine target hardware: Pi Zero 2W = Cortex-A53 ARMv8-A, hardware VFPv4+NEON — use f32. RP2040 = Cortex-M0+ thumbv6m-none-eabi, NO FPU — use u16 fixed-point (0-65535 = 0.0-1.0). Do NOT conflate Pi Zero 2W with original Pi Zero (BCM2835 ARMv6 soft-float). [2026-03-10]

JXL (JPEG XL) accepted as native Styrene image format. Key factors: best compression at ≤50KB (mesh sweet spot), lossless JPEG repack (unique — 20% smaller, bit-exact reversible), progressive decode for slow links, pure Rust decoder (jxl-oxide 0.12, actively maintained), clean BSD-3 license. WebP rejected (less efficient at ≤50KB, no JPEG repack, pure Rust zenwebp only 0.3). AVIF rejected (patent complexity, 3x slower ARM decode, fragmented Rust crates). JPEG accepted as universal fallback.

Image format alternatives assessment completed and documented at styrene-rs/docs/image-format-assessment.md. Rejected: HEIF (patents, no Rust), AVIF (patent complexity, slow ARM decode, fragmented Rust), QOI (worse than JPEG at ≤50KB), FLIF (dead), BPG (dead, H.265 patents), WebP (not best at ≤50KB, no JPEG repack, less mature pure Rust). WebP and JPEG remain accepted receive formats.

PyO3 hybrid daemon approach accepted to supersede 'no FFI, no PyO3 bindings' stance. Enables incremental module-by-module migration from Python to Rust within the running styrened daemon, with per-module compatibility verification via dual-path test fixtures (same tests run against both Python and Rust implementations).

Rust migration phased: Phase 1 (data layer, no RNS coupling) — styrene_wire.py, node_store.py, mesh_device.py, conversation_service.py. Phase 2 (crypto/protocol) — pqc_session.py, file_transfer.py, rns_service.py. Phase 3 (RNS integration) — reticulum.py, lxmf_service.py. Never port: TUI, config, doctor, CLI, auto_reply.

TAP-over-RNS.Link tunnel lifecycle must be managed by a privileged sidecar or via styrened.nix granting AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_ADMIN to the styrened service unit — two viable paths: (1) extend styrened.nix with AmbientCapabilities + pyroute2 netlink calls in Python, (2) a separate 'styrene-tunnel' helper binary (setuid or systemd PrivilegedGroup) that styrened communicates with over a Unix socket.

macOS nodes (operator workstations) participate in the mesh via RNS over TCP (tier 1 WireGuard gateway path), not via batman-adv. WireGuard to a gateway node bridges into bat0 for IP access. RNS.Link L2 tunneling reserved for LoRa-only nodes with no IP path — the gap WireGuard can't fill.

Mesh VPN tier 1 implementation: use RNS.Link (DirectLinkService) to exchange WireGuard keys and endpoints, then WireGuard handles IP traffic. Gateway nodes bridge wg-styrene into bat0 via batctl. Mac connects via WireGuard to gateway, no batman-adv needed on macOS.

Mesh IP space uses IPv6 ULA (RFC 4193) fd73:7479:7265:6e65::/64. Each node derives its /128 from SHA-256 of RNS identity hash — stable, collision-free, works point-to-point or with BATMAN gateway. When gateway present: Macs route full /64 through it into bat0. When gateway dies: direct /128 routes still work (graceful degradation to point-to-point).

macOS mesh VPN privilege model: call sudo wg-quick up once at VPN start (triggers password prompt at most once per 5min window), then use wg set peer without sudo for all per-peer operations. This avoids repeated prompts as mesh nodes come online.

Mesh VPN handshake uses LXMF protocol (VPN_HANDSHAKE_REQUEST 0x34/VPN_HANDSHAKE_RESPONSE 0x35) not DirectLink RNS.Link requests — hub routes signaling as store-and-forward, no O(n²) direct links needed. Implemented and released in v0.13.33.

Fix for DirectLinkService path discovery: announce the datalink destination via RNS so peers can discover it, OR reuse the operator path since both destinations share the same identity. Currently investigating adding announce call in _setup_datalink_destination().

Capability implemented as a class with ClassVar[str] constants (not Enum) — string values like 'rpc.exec' for config readability, ClassVar pattern avoids descriptor protocol issues with frozenset construction.

upgrade screen scrollbar: overflow-y auto (not scroll) prevents forced scrollbar when content fits; scrollbar-size-vertical:1, scrollbar-color:$panel on $surface background. changelog-title uses $primary-lighten-1 not $panel.

Mesh enclave membership is NOT self-advertised in announces — doing so would defeat anonymity for nodes that want to remain pseudonymous on shared transports. Classification as "my mesh" vs "other/unknown" is derived solely from local RBAC roster membership. An optional out-of-band INFO_REQUEST can be sent to unknown nodes, but receiving nodes must default-deny it (same as all other inbound requests). This is NOT part of the announce protocol.

Capability data sensitivity split: status.request returns only non-identifiable metadata (styrene version, uptime, profile type, capability flags) — nothing that identifies the operator or links the node to an identity. info.request is a separate opt-in capability returning identifiable metadata (node name, operator label, enclave affiliation if chosen). This keeps passive status queries safe for default-allow while identifiable disclosure remains explicit default-deny. Applies to both RPC STATUS_REQUEST and DirectLink /status handler.

info_respond config flag (default false) on DiscoveryConfig controls whether /info DirectLink handler serves identifiable node metadata — default-deny silent empty-dict response, explicit opt-in required. operator_label field also on DiscoveryConfig.

For 'my mesh' classification, check identity_hash explicitly in RBACPolicy.roster with role >= PEER using config.rbac.resolve_role(identity_hash) — resolve_role() does prefix-match blocked first, then roster lookup, then default_role fallback, so default_role=PEER would classify all nodes as mine.

Dashboard mesh split fix strategy: store both destination_hash and identity_hash in tree node.data (e.g., as tuple or dataclass), or maintain a separate dict[destination_hash, identity_hash] on MeshDeviceTree. This is the root fix for all comparison/cache-key mismatches. Robustness and security primary focus over performance.

_format_other_line 'gave up' state: when _meta_fail_count[identity_hash] > 0 and no meta cached, no suffix is shown (pass statement). Node displays with just the truncated identity hash — no pending indicator and no error text.

Datalink response validation strategy: validate at the DirectLinkService layer (not dashboard), so all callers receive pre-sanitized dicts. _validate_meta_response/_validate_info_response are the canonical trust boundary for external node data.

Phase 3 capability tier decisions: DATALINK_PING/META/INFO added at PEER tier; DATALINK_STATUS moved from MONITOR to PEER (link-level, app-layer still gates full data to MONITOR+); DATALINK_SPEEDTEST stays at MONITOR. New _datalink_allow_mode(cap) returns (ALLOW_ALL, None) or (ALLOW_LIST, allowed_list) based on rbac.should_use_allow_all(cap). New _reregister_datalink_handlers() re-registers all 5 handlers when roster changes.

TDD approach validated for RBAC Phase 3: writing 39 tests first (27 failing) then implementing caught a real design issue — /speedtest RBAC gate denied legacy-mode callers because _datalink_rbac_role() returns PEER in legacy mode which is below MONITOR. TDD forced the correct fix (skip app-layer RBAC gate when self.config.rbac is None). User wants to increase TDD default across the board based on these results.

Relay link lifecycle: default teardown on either side disconnect; permanent links require triple consent (relay.request_permanent + hub allow_permanent config + relay.accept_permanent). Same-enclave permanent = admin self-service; cross-enclave = mutual consent from both ends.

Relay data path: channel-based multiplexed forwarding over RNS.Link (not raw request/response) — enables future port forwarding, aligns with DirectLink endpoint model. Needs verification that RNS.Channel supports bidirectional byte forwarding pattern.

Relay data path confirmed: RNS.Channel is single-packet (~383B, size-constrained) — suitable for signaling only, not bulk forwarding. Hybrid approach: Channel for relay signaling, link.request() forwarding for DirectLink endpoints (/status /ping /meta /info /speedtest), RNS.Resource proxying for bulk file transfer.

Cross-enclave dual-path architecture decided: every feature gets an LXMF message type (fire-and-forget, always works) + DirectLink endpoint (confirmed, real-time, works with direct or TURN relay). Auto-detect prefers DirectLink, falls back to LXMF. Feature RBAC is transport-independent. TURN is priority (force multiplier), LXMF paths ship in parallel, DirectLink paths light up post-TURN. New capabilities: clipboard.send/receive (PEER), discovery.peers (PEER), jobs.submit/cancel (OPERATOR), jobs.status (MONITOR). Design tree: cross-enclave-features → turn-relay + independent-cross-enclave, all decided. [2026-03-07]

Cross-enclave independent features (clipboard, discovery, jobs) assessed: TURN provides delivery confirmation, real-time freshness, progress streaming for all LXMF features. Design tree nodes independent-cross-enclave and turn-relay both marked decided. OpenSpec scaffolded at openspec/changes/turn-relay/ (proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md).

OpenSpec /assess found relay RBAC wiring gap caused by task decomposition by file-layer (models/service/integration) rather than spec-domain — RBAC enforcement scenarios from relay/rbac.md fell between group 2 (register caps) and group 3 (enforce limits). relay.reject capability is orthogonal (not in any RBAC tier), like vpn.handshake. Must be explicitly granted per-identity. This prevents every PEER from automatically having "reject relay" which would break the relay system. relay.request/list/teardown/accept remain at PEER tier. [2026-03-07]

StyreneScreen lifecycle contract decisions: (1) base class approach for all 13 internal screens, (2) StyreneLoadingIndicator subclasses Textual LoadingIndicator, (3) graceful degradation: auto-retry failed IPC, notify user after failures, log thoroughly for future debugging, (4) centralized app-level staleness timer with 'experimental' full-refresh mode for debug path.

StyreneScreen lifecycle contract fully decided: base class for all 13 screens with _load_data() (required), _cleanup(), _on_error(), _loading_message() hooks all with robust logging. Yggdrasil should NOT replace WireGuard as the VXLAN underlay (breaks tier convergence for LoRa/WiFi-only nodes) and should NOT replace enclave IPv6 subnets (no scope semantics, unavailable on air-gapped nodes). Correct role: optional NAT-busting WG endpoint source in /vpn/handshake.

Yggdrasil deployment model decided: NixOS uses services.yggdrasil (declarative, system-managed, admin-socket-only from styrened). OCI container bundles yggdrasil binary in nix build .#oci. PyPI install requires user-installed binary; styrened doctor checks. YggdrasilService abstracts all three: probes admin socket first, manages process only if socket absent and manage_process=True.

Yggdrasil peers discovered via RNS are ephemeral — not persisted to yggdrasil.conf across daemon restarts. Re-bootstrapping via the RNS virtuous cycle is intentional. Persisting dynamic peer lists introduces stale credential acceptance and RBAC revocation blindness. Static initial_peers in YggdrasilConfig (operator-configured) are the only persistent peers. Principle: trust is re-established from first principles on every restart, not assumed from cached state. [2026-03-08]

Third-party attestations are additive, opt-in, and non-coercive — A CAC, corporate PKI, or any other X.509-backed identity can sign a binding attestation: "I, holder of this verified credential, assert that this StyreneID public key is mine." That attestation travels with the identity manifest as an optional attestations[] array. Peers who trust the issuing PKI chain can verify it. Peers who don't care ignore it entirely. This is additive — it says nothing about what the peer can do on the network, only provides a verifiable claim about who they are. No Styrene peer is forced to trust any attestation chain. This is explicitly different from CAC-as-hardware-token (using the CAC device for key derivation/protection) vs. CAC-as-attestation (the DoD cert chain vouches for the StyreneID holder). Both use cases are supported and composable: a DoD operator can use their CAC as the hardware token AND publish its attestation.. See /Users/cwilson/workspace/styrene-lab/styrened/docs/styrene-identity.md, decision: Third-party attestations are additive, opt-in, and non-coercive

ABS scope is deferred — standard Styrene gets hybrid-by-default, ABS enforces PQ-mandatory — Standard Styrene: hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA-65, PQ components available but not enforced on peers. Operator discretion on trust thresholds. This prevents PQ key sizes from crippling performance on constrained links today. ABS: ML-DSA-65 mandatory for identity, minimum endorsement thresholds enforced network-side, no plaintext content to unatttested peers. The division means we don't impose future-thinking as a current limitation on standard deployments. ABS is an upgrade path, not a retrofit. The two tiers share the StyreneID primitive and the same RNS routing layer — ABS just enforces stricter application-layer policies on top of the same infrastructure.. One-step distrust model — distrust filters trust signals, never propagates independently — Directly grounded in Guha et al. 2004, the best empirical performer on real WoT data. When node A has BLOCKED node B (Tier 1) or issued/received a Tier 2 advisory about B: B's trust endorsements are discounted once before contributing to A's trust computation. Distrust does not propagate further. Independent trust paths (C endorses X without going through B) are unaffected by A's distrust of B. The alternative — propagated distrust (B = T−D, iterated) — creates pathological self-distrust cycles and is explicitly rejected by the paper. Implementation: when computing a peer's derived trust score, filter the endorsement graph to downweight edges from BLOCKED peers by one step before running the WLC propagation.. See /Users/cwilson/workspace/styrene-lab/styrened/docs/styrene-distrust-model.md, decision: One-step distrust model — distrust filters trust signals, never propagates independently

No enemy-of-my-enemy transitivity — (distrust→distrust) has no transitive meaning — The paper leaves this philosophically unresolved and identifies pathological cases. An attacker can construct Sybil nodes that loudly distrust legitimate voices hoping to trigger false trust signals via double-negation. The rule is not implemented. A's distrust of B, combined with B's distrust of C, tells A nothing about C. The only valid distrust transitivity is the one-step filter: A distrusts B → A discounts B's positive endorsements once. Negative×negative=positive is not modeled.. See /Users/cwilson/workspace/styrene-lab/styrened/docs/styrene-distrust-model.md, decision: No enemy-of-my-enemy transitivity — (distrust→distrust) has no transitive meaning

WLC propagation with γ=0.5 depth attenuation and combined atomic operators — Empirically grounded in Guha et al. 2004. Trust score uses weighted linear combination of four atomic propagation operators: direct (α₁=0.4), co-citation (α₂=0.4), transpose (α₃=0.1), trust coupling (α₄=0.1). Per-hop discount γ=0.5 (trust halves at each WoT hop). Majority rounding: a peer's trust is read from the majority label of their local trusted neighborhood, not a global statistic. This yields depth 1=100%, depth 2=50%, depth 3=25%, depth 4+=≤12.5% — beyond 4 hops the signal is noise. Co-citation weight at 0.4 (equal to direct) reflects the finding that multiple independent endorsers are as informative as a direct trust relationship.. See /Users/cwilson/workspace/styrene-lab/styrened/docs/styrene-trust-model.md, decision: WLC propagation with γ=0.5 depth attenuation and combined atomic operators

Continuous Appleseed score (not binary tiers), discretized at RBAC boundary only — Binary tiers (PGP: unknown/marginal/full) are too coarse and don't leverage the information in the endorsement graph. Continuous 0–1 Appleseed scores are the right internal representation. They naturally encode depth attenuation and co-citation weight without any threshold engineering. Discretization happens only at the RBAC boundary: the TUI displays the continuous score and suggests tier assignments, but the operator maps to RBAC roles explicitly. Threshold consensus (m-of-n) is still valid as a UI heuristic — "3 of your OPERATOR contacts endorse this peer" is a useful prompt — but it's not how the score is computed internally. Grounded in Guha 2004 (co-citation weight = 0.4) and Appleseed (spreading activation is inherently continuous).. See /Users/cwilson/workspace/styrene-lab/styrened/docs/styrene-trust-model.md, decision: Continuous Appleseed score (not binary tiers), discretized at RBAC boundary only

Endorsements are encrypted-in-transit, operator-controlled publication, DP aggregate — Three-level privacy model that avoids PGP's public-graph mistake while still enabling useful trust propagation: (1) Individual endorsement edges are only revealed when a peer explicitly fetches your manifest — not broadcast, not gossiped. (2) Operators choose whether to include endorsements in their public manifest at all (default: included, opt-out to suppress). (3) Aggregate trust scores published by hubs use differential privacy noise injection (ITCS 2025 framework: (ε,δ,G)-TGDP) to prevent social graph inference from the published scores. (4) Future Phase 3: ZK trust proofs (zk-eigentrust pattern) allow proving "score ≥ threshold" without revealing graph structure. This gives a mathematically principled spectrum from "fully private" to "DP-private" to "fully public" rather than a binary choice.. See /Users/cwilson/workspace/styrene-lab/styrened/docs/styrene-trust-model.md, decision: Endorsements are encrypted-in-transit, operator-controlled publication, DP aggregate

EigenTrust Layer 3 pre-trusted vector seeded from OPERATOR+ RBAC roster — EigenTrust power iteration requires a pre-trusted peer seed vector. Without it the algorithm defaults to uniform trust — meaningless. For hub-computed Layer 3, the pre-trusted vector is: resolve_role(h) >= Role.OPERATOR → weight=1.0, all others → 0.0. This maps directly onto the existing RBAC system, produces personalized hub scores, and is only changed by explicit operator roster mutation. Grounded in the original Kamvar 2003 paper's security analysis: pre-trusted set must be small, well-known, and non-compromisable. The OPERATOR+ roster satisfies all three properties by design..
