CTAP2 canonical CBOR for all signed manifest and endorsement structures — RFC 8949 §4.2 defines multiple incompatible canonical forms (CDE, CTAP2 canonical, old canonical). COSE signatures are canonical-form-sensitive — a signature computed over CTAP2-canonical CBOR will not verify against a CDE-encoded payload. Since StyreneID manifest signing must be compatible with YubiKey PIV and hardware-backed FIDO2 keys, which already implement CTAP2 canonical CBOR, we declare CTAP2 canonical as the wire protocol constant for all signed structures. All verifiers must normalize to CTAP2 canonical before signature verification. This is documented in the wire protocol spec as a constant, not left implementation-defined.. f32 for all daemon and Pi-class targets; u16 fixed-point for bare-metal MCU only — Pi Zero 2W is Cortex-A53 (ARMv8-A) with hardware VFPv4 + NEON — f32/f64 arithmetic is hardware-accelerated. Only the RP2040 (Cortex-M0+, thumbv6m-none-eabi) genuinely lacks an FPU and requires software float emulation (~10× slower). The trust score type is therefore f32 for all Rust daemon builds targeting Linux/aarch64/armhf. A u16 fixed-point representation (0–65535 = 0.0–1.0) is used only for the bare-metal MCU port where the target triple is thumbv6m-none-eabi or similar no-FPU targets. The γ=0.5 attenuation step is a right-shift in fixed-point, which is free on any processor including Cortex-M0+.. Trust propagation model (Guha et al. 2004 / Epinions): one-step distrust only (never propagates beyond 1 hop, no double-negative=trust rule). WLC: α=(0.4 direct, 0.4 co-citation, 0.1 transpose, 0.1 trust-coupling), γ=0.5 per-hop decay. Derive trust from local trusted neighborhood majority. Distrust sparsity (85/15 ratio) is load-bearing. Design nodes: styrene-trust-model, styrene-distrust-model. OpenSpec styrene-distrust-model is planned (v0.17.0).

pipx upgrade styrene to 0.10.45 upgrades the meta-package but leaves styrened at 0.10.40 in the venv — pip's default --upgrade-strategy=only-if-needed doesn't pull transitive deps when the constraint (~=0.10) is already satisfied. The eager strategy fix in 0.10.45 is a catch-22: users need 0.10.45 installed to get the fix that would have installed 0.10.45.

Chat incremental refresh message deletion now handled: if old_ids_set - new_ids_set is non-empty (messages deleted), resets _message_ids and _last_displayed_date and triggers full rebuild instead of silently leaving ghost bubbles.
NodeInfoPanel _load_comms_data() contact_count fixed: replaced nonexistent get_contacts() with get_all_nodes() from NodeStore. contact_count now reflects known mesh nodes in standalone mode.

_load_comms_data() local_hash=None guard fixed: when local_hash is None, both source_hash and destination_hash are added to peer_hashes set (conservative overcount) rather than always adding source_hash.
align-vertical:bottom removed from #chat-message-container in imperial_crt.tcss — property was confirmed non-functional for scrollable overflow containers and has been deleted.
align-vertical:bottom removed from #chat-message-container CSS. Property was confirmed to do nothing for overflow scroll containers in Textual. Scroll gravity achieved only via scroll_end() calls.
_update_optimistic_status was fixed to match outgoing bubbles by content (raw_content comparison) rather than just reversed position, preventing wrong-bubble updates on concurrent sends.
_stage_clipboard_attachment dead guard (unreachable 'if attachment is not None') removed; also fixed indentation regression from the removal.
Exploration table empty-state row now renders message in NAME column (first column) with empty strings for remaining columns, instead of '-' placeholders with message in STATUS column.
Chat input bar separator border changed from 'heavy' to 'wide' in imperial_crt.tcss for broader terminal compatibility.
MeshDevice.hops field persistence fixed in v0.13.1: hops column added via ALTER TABLE migration to NodeStore, included in save_node() INSERT/UPDATE, read back in _row_to_device().
_load_comms_data() SQL blocking fixed in v0.13.1: replaced .all() with SQL aggregate queries, no rows loaded into Python memory.
_load_comms_data() refactored in v0.13.1 to use SQL aggregates (func.count, case) instead of loading all rows — no longer blocks event loop on large message history.

_fetch_daemon_status IPC calls parallelized in v0.13.1: conversations, contacts, and auto_reply launched as asyncio.create_task concurrently, all runs use group='dashboard-status' to prevent concurrent worker races.
Multiple concurrent _fetch_daemon_status workers fixed in v0.13.1: all run_worker() calls use group='dashboard-status', ensuring only one worker runs at a time.

_stage_from_clipboard() main-thread fix fully applied in v0.13.1: renamed to _do_stage_from_clipboard(), all callers (on_paste, action_paste_attachment) call it synchronously on main thread. NSPasteboard threading bug resolved in all chat clipboard code paths.
NSPasteboard threading bug fixed in v0.13.1: _do_stage_from_clipboard() called synchronously from action handlers and on_paste (main thread), never inside run_worker or asyncio tasks.

TRAFFIC section in NodeInfoPanel IPC mode partially fixed in v0.13.1: messages_received now populated from message_count total; sent/pending remain 0 pending IPC endpoint changes for per-direction breakdown.

RNS announce callback does not receive the receiving interface — interface info must be read post-hoc from RNS.Transport.path_table[destination_hash][5] after the callback fires, which may reflect a different announce's winner if multiple hubs compete.

v0.13.2 released: fix VIA column in exploration/dashboard now shows 'Interface Name → next_hop_hash' (e.g., 'Styrene Community Hub → a3f6f4c8') to disambiguate which transport node relayed an announce when multiple hubs are connected.

Dashboard VIA column showed local interface name only (e.g., 'Styrene Community Hub') for all devices — fixed in v0.13.2: discovered_via now includes next-hop transport hash suffix (e.g., 'Styrene Community Hub → a3f6f4c8'), disambiguating which transport node relayed announces when multiple peers are enabled.

Dashboard mesh devices grouped under a single interface name — partially improved in v0.13.2 by adding next-hop hash suffix to VIA label; most announces legitimately arrive through Styrene Community Hub (best connectivity), but the suffix now shows which specific transport node relayed each.
Settings screen stacked on repeated backtick press — fixed in v0.13.4: action_push_screen_settings now checks isinstance(self.screen, SettingsScreen) and returns early if already on top.

Chat send failure while node is actively announcing: LXMF delivery failures can occur even when destination is visible in mesh because path establishment and announce propagation are decoupled — path may not be established despite announce arriving. No UI explanation of this to the user.

send_message returns None causing retry failures when the peer's identity is not in RNS cache or NodeStore — _resolve_identity() exhausts all 4 strategies. This is the primary cause of both initial send failures and retry failures when destination is unreachable.

ChatWidget Phase 3 retry design: R binding calls action_retry_message → auto-selects last failed bubble if none selected → _retry_single(message_id). ctrl+r retries all failed with per-message groups. _retry_after_refresh handles message_id=0 optimistic bubbles by refreshing from DB first. message_id=0 optimistic bubble issue now addressed.
action_retry_all_failed was silently cancelling all-but-last retry workers because all used group='chat-retry'. Fixed: each retry worker now uses group='chat-retry-{message_id}'.
Failed messages now show red ✗ + '↻ press R to retry' hint on the line below. R key auto-selects last failed message if none is selected. Still no clickable button — keyboard-only affordance.

Chat failure/retry system partially fixed: R now auto-selects last failed bubble without requiring Tab+navigation; optimistic bubbles (id=0) trigger _retry_after_refresh() which refreshes from DB first. User still needs to know R key exists — no inline UI affordance yet. Footer shows 'R Retry' only when ChatWidget (not Input) has focus.

_update_optimistic_status for attachment-only messages (empty content) was broken — content matching skipped empty string, so it matched wrong or no bubble. Fixed: empty content matches most recent pending outgoing bubble instead of content-matching.

After send failure, optimistic bubble (message_id=0) was never replaced with real DB record because _refresh_messages() was not called on the failure path. Fixed: both TimeoutError and generic Exception paths now call _refresh_messages() after 0.3s delay.

send_message returns None when RNS.Identity.recall() evicts the identity cache for a recently-announcing peer — identity was stored during announce processing but cache flushed before send. Root cause of 'Server c0cd' chat send failures despite active announces.

_resolve_identity Strategy 5 (path request + 10s blocking poll) blocks the IPC handler thread. Since async IPC handlers call synchronous send_message() directly (not in an executor), this risks blocking the asyncio event loop if ever called from coroutine context without thread isolation.

UpgradeScreen changelog implemented in progress: WHAT'S NEW panel added to UpgradeScreen showing changes between current and latest. fetch_changelog() in tui/services/changelog.py uses local git log → GitHub API → PyPI version list fallback chain. GitHub compare API fails for private repo without auth; git log strategy added to resolve.
fetch_changelog() GitHub compare API strategy fails for private repos without auth token — git log strategy (now Strategy 1) resolves this for local git checkouts.

Pages tab in MeshDeviceDetailScreen was incorrectly shown for all devices in v0.13.9 — corrected in same session to only show for NomadNet nodes or devices whose RNS identity also has a NomadNet announce (via node store lookup by identity_hash).

CMD_PAGE_REGENERATE IPC command implemented: CmdPageRegenerateRequest in messages.py, handle_cmd_page_regenerate() in handlers.py, page_regenerate_index() in client.py, registered in server.py dispatch table. PageServerService.regenerate_index() is now exposed via IPC.

fetch_changelog() PyPI fallback (Strategy 4 previously Strategy 3) fired for pipx users because the package is not installed from a git checkout, returning only version numbers with no commit messages — anemic changelog. Fixed in v0.13.13 by embedding _changelog.py at build time (Strategy 1).
page_server.py 'About Styrene' section fixed in v0.13.12: docs URL corrected to https://docs.styrene.io (was /styrened/api/ subdirectory), install recommendation changed to 'pipx install styrene'.
public-hub justfile had STYRENED_VERSION hardcoded to 0.10.21 in the build recipe (not just Containerfile default ARG) — both locations must be kept in sync when bumping versions. Fixed for 0.13.13.

Pages tab missing in MeshDeviceDetailScreen when navigating from StyreneFleetTable (Styrene tab in ExplorationScreen) — _resolve_nomadnet_destination() fails to find the NomadNet announce entry because the hub's NomadNet destination hash differs from the Styrene node hash, requiring identity_hash-based NodeStore lookup that may not be finding the entry.

_resolve_nomadnet_destination() searched only NodeStore but NomadNet and Styrene on the same hub use different RNS identities (separate ~/.nomadnetwork/storage/identity vs ~/.styrene/identity), so identity_hash matching across sibling aspects never finds a match. Live discovered_devices is also unchecked in IPC mode (always empty). Root cause: identity_hash assumption is wrong for multi-process hubs.

_resolve_nomadnet_destination() resolution order: (1) device is NOMADNET_NODE directly, (2) device advertises 'pages' capability — compute NomadNet destination from RNS.Identity.recall + RNS.Destination.hash, (3) NodeStore identity_hash cross-match. Strategy 2 only works when styrened owns the destination (same identity). Hub multi-process case now fixed via 8th announce field (nomadnet_dest).

Multiple unit test files (test_announce_fingerprint.py, test_daemon_announce.py, test_parse_announce_autoreply.py, test_short_name.py) have stale tuple unpacking expecting 7-element returns from parse_announce_data() — failing after 8-tuple extension with nomadnet_dest field. Being fixed incrementally with sed replacements.

Upgrade screen WHAT'S NEW changelog empty for pipx installs FIXED in v0.13.15: new Strategy 2 downloads the target version's wheel from PyPI (~200KB), extracts its _changelog.py via zipfile, and parses entries. Target version's bundled changelog always covers itself and prior versions.

UpgradeScreen changelog fully fixed in v0.13.15: Strategy 2 (_fetch_from_pypi_wheel) downloads target version's wheel from PyPI and extracts _changelog.py — works for all install methods including pipx. Strategy 1 (bundled) still fires first for cases where installed version already has the entries.

_resolve_nomadnet_destination() adds hub capability heuristic in v0.13.15: if device has 'pages' capability, use its own destination_hash optimistically — page browser handles connection errors. Hub capability ('hub') alone is NOT used; only 'pages' capability triggers this fallback.

Hub pages capability fix shipped in v0.13.16: daemon now probes NomadNet identity files directly (including /app/.nomadnetwork/storage/identity) regardless of page_server.enabled, adds 'pages' capability and nomadnet_dest to announce even in multi-process hub mode.

v0.13.16 fix: caps_str was generated before NomadNet identity probe, so dynamically added 'pages' capability was not included in the announce wire format. Fixed by moving caps_str join after the NomadNet block.

Pages tab in MeshDeviceDetailScreen was missing for hub v0.13.15 because page_server.is_started gate prevented NomadNet identity probe. Fixed in v0.13.16 which probes NomadNet identity files directly regardless of page_server.enabled.

Micron renderer in page_browser produces anemic output: headings are just bold with no color, links have no color differentiation, no visual hierarchy. Improvement in progress — adding colored heading styles (#5af0ce h1, #3fbfa0 h2, #6a9a8e h3).

public-hub NomadNet pages (index.mu, connect.mu, about.mu, docs/) are persisted on the nomadnet-data PVC, not baked into the image — they were created manually in a previous session. Only demo/ pages are copied from the image at startup.

Micron color codes `Fg5af0ce (6-char hex foreground) were being misread as grayscale when prefixed with extra characters. The correct format is `Fg50 for grayscale-50 or `F + 6-char hex for named color. Renderer now emits correct Rich markup for h1 (#5af0ce), h2 (#3fbfa0), h3 (#6a9a8e) headings and cyan (#5ac8fa) clickable links.

UpgradeScreen 'Restart TUI' button removed in v0.13.18 — _finish_success() now auto-dismisses with True immediately after daemon kill, triggering automatic TUI restart with no user interaction required.

Pages tab in MeshDeviceDetailScreen shows correct destination hash (af1ec9...) but page requests time out on /page/demo/index.mu — page browser cannot fetch from hub's NomadNet destination despite correct hash resolution.

NomadNet announces from the hub's own NomadNet process do NOT get delivered to styrened's announce handler because they share the same RNS instance — RNS does not deliver local announces to local handlers. Remote nodes receive the announce over the network normally.

Page browser 'Page request timed out' error on first attempt is transient — NomadNet destination path not yet cached in local daemon. Subsequent attempts after path caches succeed. Confirmed working end-to-end: /page/index.mu returns 963 bytes from hub's NomadNet.

Page browser 'Link establishment failed' error observed in TUI despite end-to-end page fetch working in standalone Python test — root cause under investigation: daemon's shared RNS instance may have different link establishment behavior than standalone RNS.Reticulum() client instances.

Page browser 'Link establishment failed' debugging: added INFO-level logging to page_browser.py _get_or_create_link() — logs path found + identity recall result, link object creation with initial status, and ESTABLISHED/CLOSED callback events including teardown_reason. Released in v0.13.19 to diagnose daemon vs standalone RNS link behavior difference.

asyncio.Future() in _get_or_create_link() is created without explicit loop parameter — in Python 3.10+ this binds to the running loop. If RNS callbacks fire from a different thread (RNS uses daemon threads), run_coroutine_threadsafe scheduling onto self._event_loop is correct but requires _event_loop to be captured correctly at service start.

PageBrowserService fetch_page() fails intermittently with INITIATOR_CLOSED (teardown_reason=2) — confirmed transient: same test code fails then succeeds on re-run. Root cause may be stale path entries after hub reconnection storm or RNS state from previous instances.

PageBrowserService works correctly when run standalone with asyncio.run() + asyncio.Future + run_coroutine_threadsafe pattern — all link establishment patterns tested and functional in isolation. The intermittent failure in the TUI daemon context is not a code correctness issue.

Hub RNS config has 10 TCPClientInterface peers (Dublin, BetweenTheBorders, ON6ZQ, Beleth, Chicago Nomad, Acehoss, Quad4, Interloper, g00n Dallas, Loopback) — any peer cycling its TCP connection triggers id() change detection, producing the reconnect storm logged in hub pods.
public-hub build cached old styrened version (0.13.16) despite Containerfile updated to 0.13.20 — pip layer was cached. Requires --no-cache flag on podman build to force fresh pip install.

Hub TCP reconnect debounce in v0.13.20 does not suppress 're-announce' triggers — _handle_reconnection calls are debounced but log messages and re-announce still fire ~20/10s on the hub. 'churn suppressed' log never appears, indicating the debounce path is not being hit.

_finish_success() in UpgradeScreen kills daemon then attempts to start new daemon via _start_daemon() before TUI re-exec — _start_daemon() uses shutil.which('styrened') which may not find the binary in pipx venv PATH, causing silent failure and TUI re-launch into DaemonSetupScreen. Under investigation in v0.13.21.

After successful upgrade (v0.13.21), TUI kills old daemon, attempts to start new daemon via Popen, then re-execs. If shutil.which('styrened') fails to locate the binary (pipx venv PATH issue), daemon never starts and re-launched TUI shows DaemonSetupScreen instead of connecting to running daemon.

Hub TCP interface churn: Hub with many TCPClientInterface peers (10+) sees rapid interface object recreation by RNS. The id(iface) tracking in _check_interface_states() detects these as reconnections. Fixed with 30s debounce in v0.13.20, but root cause is RNS recreating interface objects during normal operation.

PageCacheService._crawl_loop() has a 60-second initial sleep before the first crawl refresh — no immediate crawl on start. Background refresh only fires for saved sites past their refresh_interval (default 3600s). Sites never refresh until their interval elapses.

IPC handler for CMD_PAGE_FETCH has write-through caching and fallback: on status=='ok' calls cache_svc.cache_page(); on non-ok status checks cache_svc.get_cached_page() and adds cached_content/cached_at/cached_content_length to the response dict. The TUI widget reads these fields in _load_page() correctly.

Page cache tables (page_cache, saved_sites) are created via Base.metadata.create_all(engine) in daemon._start_page_browser() using init_db(). They do NOT use the ALTER TABLE migration pattern used by other NodeStore columns — they require the SQLAlchemy models to be present when init_db() first runs. Existing installs that previously ran init_db() without these models will have the tables missing until their DB is re-created or migrations run explicitly.
_start_daemon in upgrade.py and _auto_start_daemon in app.py are duplicate implementations of the same shutil.which + Popen pattern — must keep both in sync.
Background _crawl_loop has no circuit breaker for database errors — SQLite lock/corruption causes repeated warnings every 5 minutes forever.
No IPC handler tests for five new page cache commands (save/remove/list/crawl/get_cached). No test for write-through cache integration in IPC handler. No test for reconnect debounce timing.
page_cache has no eviction policy or TTL enforcement — cache grows unbounded. The PageResponse.cache_ttl field parsed from micron #!c=N header is never used by PageCacheService.

Reconnect debounce is global (single _last_reconnect_time) not per-interface — a reconnect on interface A suppresses all reconnects on other interfaces for the full 30s window, potentially silently dropping legitimate re-announces.
No CMD_PAGE_CLEAR_CACHE command exists — users cannot clear cached pages from the TUI or IPC.
crawl_site() fires sequential fetch_page requests with no delay between pages — holds RNS.Link open for the entire crawl; no backoff on link drop mid-crawl.

Three separate SQLAlchemy engines created to same SQLite file in daemon (lines 398, 1043, 1208 of daemon.py) — three connection pools sharing one SQLite file risks 'database is locked' errors during concurrent crawl+message writes.

Adversarial code review (v0.13.23) found: crawl IPC timeout (fixed fire-and-forget), _last_reconnect_time uninit (fixed), global debounce suppresses all interfaces for 30s window, unbounded cache growth no eviction, no CMD_PAGE_CLEAR_CACHE, no IPC handler tests for 5 new page cache commands, _start_daemon duplicated in upgrade.py and app.py.

CMD_PAGE_CRAWL_SITE IPC handler confirmed fire-and-forget in v0.13.24: asyncio.create_task launches crawl_site() in background and returns {started:true} immediately. Crawl progress not observable via IPC.

CMD_PAGE_CRAWL_SITE IPC handler fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task fixed in v0.13.24 (was v0.13.23 partial fix in handlers.py only). Returns {started:true} immediately, bypassing 30s IPC timeout.
_load_page exception handler now attempts cache fallback as of v0.13.24 — queries bridge.page_get_cached() before showing error. Only fails silently if bridge is None.

_load_page exception handler now attempts cache fallback via bridge.page_get_cached() on IPC-level failures (fixed v0.13.24). Fallback works for both daemon non-ok responses AND connection/timeout exceptions when bridge is available.
_last_reconnect_time initialized to 0.0 in RNSService.__init__ as of v0.13.24; getattr fallback removed from _check_interface_states(). Fixed.
crawl_site() BFS queue switched from list.pop(0) to collections.deque.popleft() in v0.13.24 — O(1) dequeue. Fixed.
page_cache.py: PageResponse unused import removed, quoted type annotation unquoted, f-string without placeholder removed — all fixed in v0.13.24.

Status tab redesign complete: Refresh button removed, DeviceStatusWidget now two-column cascade-colored layout showing announce data (NODE/MESH) and RPC+link enrichment (LINK/SYSTEM/NETWORK). Hub uptime=0/ip=127.0.0.1 shown with dim color to indicate useless-but-real K8s values.

Default speedtest payload sizes [256B→256KB] are LoRa-unsafe: 256KB at SF10=36min, SF12=2hr. PATH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT=15s and LINK_ESTABLISHMENT_TIMEOUT=15s are too short for multi-hop LoRa (needs 30-60s). REQUEST_TIMEOUT=10s is tight for LoRa. IPC speedtest timeout (120s) covers only ~2 payloads at SF9. No adaptive sizing, no progress reporting, no inter-test duty-cycle delay. BEING FIXED in current session.
MeshDeviceTree/exploration tables show 1725+ LXMF nodes, almost all STALE/LOST, drowning useful signal — UI filtering work in progress (hide-lost default, dim-stale, status counts bar).

Exploration LXMF tab drowning in STALE/LOST nodes (1725+ observed). Fix in progress: hide_lost=True by default, hide_stale toggle, status count bar. ReticumAnnounceTable and StyreneFleetTable getting toggle_hide_lost()/toggle_hide_stale() methods and status_counts property.

IPC command collision FIXED: CMD_DATALINK_ESTABLISH/TEARDOWN/STATUS/QUERY were 0x50-0x53, aliasing CMD_TERMINAL_OPEN/INPUT/RESIZE/CLOSE. Datalink commands moved to 0x60-0x64 range; terminal commands remain at 0x50-0x53. No more IntEnum deduplication shadowing.

_STATUS_CACHE in mesh_device_detail.py had unbounded growth — FIXED: now capped at 64 entries (_STATUS_CACHE_MAX=64), evicts oldest on overflow, and removes expired entries on read in _get_cached_status().

_auto_fetch_status cache-hit path comment 'Still try to refresh in background' was false — FIXED: got_status is no longer set on cache hit, so datalink and LXMF fetch paths still execute for a fresh update. Cached data shows immediately, then is replaced with fresh data.

DirectLinkService._resolve future race fixed: set_result/set_exception wrapped in try/except asyncio.InvalidStateError instead of checking future.done() first — eliminates concurrent resolution window.

Concurrency guard added to speedtest: DirectLinkService._speedtest_lock (asyncio.Lock created on start()) prevents concurrent speedtests — returns {status: busy} immediately if lock already held. _run_speedtest_inner() holds the lock for the duration.

Speedtest ASCII bar chart in DeviceStatusWidget now scales relative to peak result (max_kbps) not hardcoded 1000kbps — bar_len = int(kbps/max_kbps*20), giving meaningful visual differentiation across all link speeds.
DirectLinkService.stop() now called in daemon.stop() — shutdown sequence stops direct link service before page server, sets _direct_link_service to None, logs errors gracefully.

NodeInfoPanel RETICULUM section 'peers' count reflects RNS interface count (physical interfaces), not mesh device count. The STYRENE MESH count is now correct (fixed: uses node_store + live + dedup, same as MeshDeviceTree).

NodeInfoPanel MESH count fixed (v0.13.28+): now uses merged node_store.get_styrene_nodes() + discover_devices() + _deduplicate_by_identity(), matching the data source used by MeshDeviceTree. Label changed from 'peers' to 'nodes', RNS 'no peers' changed to 'no interfaces'.

NodeInfoPanel MESH node count mismatch FIXED: now uses same data source as MeshDeviceTree (merged node_store.get_styrene_nodes() + discover_devices() + _deduplicate_by_identity()), so stored/historical nodes are included in the count.

WG allowed-ips routing gap: Macs use /128 per direct peer (IPv6 ULA) but need to switch to fd73:7479:7265:6e65::/64 via gateway when a Linux gateway joins, and revert to /128 when gateway dies. Dynamic route promotion/demotion not yet implemented in MeshVPNService._configure_peer().

MeshDevice.last_seen_display appends announce count without space: `seen += f"×{device.announce_count}"` produces '4s agox8' instead of '4s ago ×8'. Two issues: missing space before ×, and × (U+00D7) may not render in SVG export font. File: models/mesh_device.py area around last_seen_display property.
Dashboard 'c' key calls action_open_chat which requires a device selected in MeshDeviceTree — silently fails (no notification, no error) when tree has no selected leaf node with identity data.
mesh_vpn.py: _detect_local_endpoint uses socket.connect(8.8.8.8) which returns LAN IP — useless for internet peers. Users must set endpoint manually with no documentation or error.
mesh_vpn.py: handle_handshake is called from RNS thread while _peers dict is accessed from asyncio thread — no lock. CPython GIL protects simple gets/sets but compound operations are a race.
mesh_vpn.py: No IPC commands for VPN status or handshake trigger — TUI cannot observe or control mesh VPN state.
mesh_vpn.py: No firewall rule added in styrened.nix for WireGuard UDP listen_port (51820) — connections silently dropped on NixOS fleet devices with default firewall.

wcswidth('●') returns 1 (same as len) — the alignment drift from Unicode symbols is a terminal/font rendering issue not fixable via wcwidth. rich.cells.cell_len() matches Rich's actual rendering, making it the correct choice.

Bug fixes from tui-bug-handoff.zip: (1) '4s ago×8' spacing fixed (space added before ×, × character preserved as U+00D7). (2) NodeInfoPanel two-column drift: `rich.cells.cell_len()` replaces `wcwidth.wcswidth()` for accurate width measurement; module-level `import re` and `from rich.cells import cell_len as rich_cell_len` moved out of hot loop. (3) HighlightedPanel on_resize: width-change guard restored — height-only redraws are no-ops since borders depend only on width.
Regression tests for tui-bug-handoff written at tests/unit/test_tui_bug_handoff.py — covers Bug 1 (announce count spacing '4s ago ×8') and Bug 3 (rich_cell_len usage for two-column alignment).

mesh_vpn.py bugs itemized in v0.13.28 session are now partially addressed: double @dataclass on MeshVPNConfig fixed, subnet_prefix default mismatch ('10.73' vs 'fd73:7479:7265:6e65') fixed in services/config.py loader.
Capture script in tui-bug-handoff uses 'c' key which opens chat/contacts shortcut, not 'b' — contacts screen never opens. Bug 2 is a test script issue, not a TUI defect.

NodeInfoPanel two-column alignment fix implemented: render() now returns a Rich Table (Table.grid) instead of str with manual padding — Rich's layout engine measures column widths during render, eliminating all Unicode width drift. Table.grid(padding=(0,2)), min_width=42 on left column, Text.from_markup() for each cell.

NodeInfoPanel column drift (Bug 3) FIXED: render() now returns Rich Table instead of manual col_width=44 string padding — Rich measures widths internally, immune to Unicode ambiguity. Tests updated to use _render_panel() helper (Rich Console capture) since render() returns RenderableType not str.
test_rns_online_no_interfaces_shows_no_peers now asserts 'no interfaces' (updated in session) — test was stale asserting 'no peers' before the label text changed.

HighlightedPanel border overflow (Bug 4) root-cause traced: math is correct (inner_width+2 == panel width), so visual overflow in screenshots is an SVG font-metrics artifact with box-drawing characters — not fixable at the Python/CSS code level.

HighlightedPanel border rendering root cause confirmed and fixed: on_mount fires with width=0 (widget not laid out), on_resize width guard then skips first valid resize. Fixed via call_after_refresh() + guard extended to catch 0→nonzero width transition.
DeviceDetailScreen SELECT DEVICE panel (Bug 5) FIXED in v0.13.31 — HighlightedPanel mount-time race fixed; provision.py placeholder Static removed (not needed).
HighlightedPanel bottom-right border overflow (Bug 4) FIXED in v0.13.31 — on_mount uses call_after_refresh() to avoid width=0 race; on_resize re-renders when width transitions from 0 to non-zero.

HighlightedPanel on_resize guard extended: re-renders when width changes OR when width transitions from 0 to non-zero (first valid layout after mount-time zero-size). on_mount uses call_after_refresh().
Dashboard 'c' key action_open_chat() now notifies user 'Select a device in the mesh tree first.' when no tree node is selected, instead of silently doing nothing.
HighlightedPanel on_resize: call_after_refresh() on mount + guard for 0→nonzero transition — borders rendered exactly once after first valid layout. No unnecessary re-renders on height-only resizes.
mesh_vpn.py cryptography dependency FIXED: 'cryptography>=41.0' added to pyproject.toml core dependencies.

mesh_vpn.py self._identity_hash crash FIXED: _start_mesh_vpn() now calls get_operator_identity_object() directly to obtain identity_hash instead of referencing the non-existent self._identity_hash attribute.
mesh_vpn.py fixes in progress: identity_hash AttributeError fixed, cryptography dep added, rsplit prefix extraction replaced with ipaddress-based extract_prefix() helper function.

mesh_vpn.py: parse_handshake_response() now checks for 'error' key before field validation — raises ValueError('Handshake rejected: {error}') on subnet_prefix_mismatch or other errors. Version field validation also added to both parse functions.

mesh_vpn.py subnet prefix extraction FIXED: replaced rsplit-based approach with extract_prefix() helper using ipaddress.IPv6Network — handles compressed IPv6, zero groups, all forms correctly. extract_prefix(mesh_ip, prefix_len) uses IPv6Network.network_address.exploded and takes first N groups based on prefix_len//16.

mesh_vpn.py: _create_interface_linux() and _create_interface_macos() now check for required binaries (ip/wg on Linux, wg-quick on macOS) via shutil.which() and return False with error log if missing. macOS wg-quick calls now use sudo prefix.

mesh_vpn.py: _create_interface() now returns bool and _start() logs 'degraded mode' warning on False — failure no longer silently passes. _create_interface_linux() and _create_interface_macos() both return bool and propagate failure reason.

mesh_vpn.py: Binary detection added in _create_interface_linux() (checks ip, wg, batctl if gateway) and _create_interface_macos() (checks wg-quick) via shutil.which() — missing binaries now produce clear error messages and return False.

mesh_vpn.py: parse_handshake_response() now checks 'error' key first and raises ValueError('Handshake rejected: {error}') — subnet_prefix_mismatch returns proper error. Both parse functions also validate HANDSHAKE_VERSION field.

mesh_vpn.py: handle_handshake() task exception now observed — loop.create_task() result stored and _on_peer_config_done() callback added via task.add_done_callback(), logging exceptions from _configure_peer().

mesh_vpn.py: No tests for handle_handshake or initiate_handshake — core handshake flow now has test_handshake_handler_rejects_prefix_mismatch and version/error-response tests. initiate_handshake flow still has zero test coverage.

mesh_vpn.py: BATMAN-ADV batctl if add wg-styrene won't work — WireGuard is L3, BATMAN-ADV hard interfaces need L2 Ethernet. FIXED: replaced direct WG→bat0 bridging with VXLAN-over-WG per-peer tunnel architecture: bat0→vxlan-<peer> (L2/UDP)→wg-styrene (L3). Each peer gets a vxlan-<hash[:10]> interface added to bat0. VNI=7379, dstport=4789, local/remote=WG mesh IPs.

mesh_vpn.py Issue 9 remaining: _peers dict accessed from RNS thread (handle_handshake) and asyncio thread (_configure_peer) — no asyncio.Lock. CPython GIL protects simple dict ops but compound read-modify-write is a race.

MeshVPNService VXLAN-over-WG: VXLAN uses WG mesh IPv6 (ULA) addresses as local/remote endpoints, but VXLAN encapsulates in UDP which must traverse the WG tunnel — sending VXLAN UDP over a WG interface whose route is only the peer's /128 works, but routing of the VXLAN multicast/broadcast frames depends on BATMAN-ADV's own MAC learning, not on WG routing. The 'dev wg-styrene' parameter roots the VXLAN in the WG interface correctly.

MeshVPNService _configure_peer() calls _create_vxlan_for_peer() only when self.config.gateway is True — non-gateway nodes never get VXLAN overlays, meaning non-gateway Linux nodes that connect to a gateway won't extend bat0 on their end. Only the gateway side creates VXLANs, leaving a half-tunnel.

VXLAN for_peer uses ALL_VXLANS share VNI=7379 — all peers share the same VNI. On the gateway, all per-peer VXLAN interfaces have the same VNI but different remote IPs (point-to-point unicast mode), which is correct. However if two peers somehow share the same VNI with different remote addresses on the same VXLAN namespace, kernel behavior varies. The point-to-point (unicast remote) configuration avoids multicast but VNI isolation between Styrene fleets using same VNI is absent.

VXLAN UDP port 4789 must be open in the firewall on Linux gateway nodes for VXLAN frames to traverse the WG tunnel — the existing styrened.nix only adds WG listen_port (51820) firewall rule issue; no VXLAN port exception is documented or implemented.

_destroy_all_vxlans() iterates self._peers but only destroys VXLANs that match entries still in _peers at teardown time. If a peer was manually removed from _peers without calling _destroy_vxlan_for_peer, the VXLAN interface leaks and is not cleaned up.

mesh_vpn.py Issue 10 FIXED: second gateway evicts first gateway's /64 allowed-ips via _update_peer_allowed_ips() before assigning /64 to new gateway. Old gateway downgraded to /128. _destroy_all_vxlans() called in stop(). _create_vxlan_for_peer() called from _configure_peer() when self.config.gateway and platform==LINUX.

mesh_vpn.py: extract_prefix returns zero-padded groups via IPv6Address.exploded (e.g., 'fd73:0079:...') but config subnet_prefix may use shortened form ('fd73:79:...'). String comparison in handshake will falsely reject peers on same subnet if config prefix isn't fully zero-padded. Normalize config prefix through extract_prefix before comparing.
mesh_vpn.py: no MTU clamping on VXLAN interfaces — VXLAN+WG adds ~110 bytes overhead, so VXLAN MTU should be ≤1330 to avoid fragmentation. LoRa-bridged links need much lower MTU. No MTU set.

mesh_vpn.py: no bat0 existence check before 'batctl meshif bat0 if add' — if batman-adv is not loaded or bat0 doesn't exist, batctl fails silently and the VXLAN interface is left up but not bridged into bat0.
mesh_vpn.py: unused import 'field' from dataclasses being removed. Also 'import field' was unused since no dataclass fields use field().

mesh_vpn.py: fd leak in _create_interface_linux() — if os.fchmod() or os.write() raises between mkstemp and os.close(fd), fd is never closed. finally block only unlinks key_path, not closes fd. Not yet fixed.

DirectLinkService.establish() identity recall fix: added RNS.Identity.recall(dest_hash_bytes, from_identity_hash=True) fallback and reordered to try recall BEFORE path discovery — avoids 45s hang when NodeStore provides identity hash instead of destination hash. Still not fully verified end-to-end.

DirectLinkService.establish() identity recall fix applied: tries recall by dest hash, then by identity hash (from_identity_hash=True), BEFORE path discovery — avoids 45s PATH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT hang when NodeStore provides identity hash. Recall result None only if identity truly unknown to daemon RNS instance (e.g., node not yet announced since daemon restart).

'L' key establish_link fix in progress: DirectLinkService.establish() now tries recall both ways (dest hash + identity hash) before path discovery. Fix not yet released. DirectLinkService.establish() fails when NodeStore has the identity but daemon has NOT received the node's announce in this RNS session — RNS.Identity.recall() returns None for identities not remembered in current session, even when NodeStore has the hash. IPC socket connection refused despite daemon running: multiple styrened processes exist (pipx auto-started daemon competes with dev venv daemon). pkill -f 'styrened daemon' kills one but another (pipx daemon) auto-restarts or was already running — lsof shows a different PID owns the socket than the dev venv process that was started. Dev venv daemon cannot claim IPC socket when pipx daemon is already running: socket file is created by pipx daemon (owned by different PID than dev venv process). The 'stale socket' removal only runs if the previous socket was truly stale, but the pipx daemon recreates it. Must use pkill -9 -f styrened to kill all instances before starting dev daemon.

DirectLinkService.establish() fails at path discovery for datalink destination: identity resolves fine but datalink dest (styrene/datalink aspect) has no path because the remote node never announces it. RNS can't establish links to unannounced destinations.

Datalink dest announce added to daemon._announce() (alongside LXMF dest) so remote nodes can discover path. But establish() still fails: local computes dest hash 1dfd10a3df4548d6 while remote announced 0f5a6232102792b2 — hash mismatch suggests different identity used. Investigating IN vs OUT vs identity discrepancy.

NodeStore has duplicate entries for styrene-node: (1) dest=9e21f49a with correct lxmf=f3e11839 and identity=698f2232, (2) dest=f3e11839 stored as operator dest with identity=698f2232 and no lxmf. Old entry dest=fe75a225 with stale identity=e012da25 also present from previous daemon run.

DirectLinkService establish() hash mismatch CONFIRMED: stale identity in NodeStore. Old operator dest fe75a225 → stale identity e012da25 → wrong datalink hash 1dfd10a3. New operator dest 9e21f49a → current identity 698f2232 → correct datalink hash. Establish to new dest works in 1.5s (RTT=230ms). Fix needed: NodeStore dedup/cleanup of old entries.

DirectLinkService establish() hash mismatch root cause confirmed: stale NodeStore data. Old operator dest (fe75a225) has old identity (e012da25); new operator dest (9e21f49a) has current identity (698f2232). Establish to new dest succeeds in 1.5s RTT=230ms. New entry: dest=9e21f49a, lxmf=f3e11839, identity=698f2232. Old operator dest fe75a225 still announces via mesh (RNS replay or second instance).

NodeStore has no mechanism to expire or merge stale entries when a device changes its RNS identity — old destination hashes persist indefinitely alongside new ones, causing TUI to show both stale and current entries for same physical node.

DirectLinkService.establish() takes LXMF destination hash, recalls identity via RNS.Identity.recall(bytes.fromhex(lxmf_dest_hash)), then computes datalink dest hash as RNS.Destination(identity, OUT, SINGLE, 'styrene', 'datalink').hash — deterministic from identity, no announce needed.

asyncio.Lock for single-inflight operations: create lock in start() as self._speedtest_lock, check .locked() for fast-reject before async with, use async with self._speedtest_lock or asyncio.Lock() as fallback.

Status cache show-stale-then-refresh pattern: on cache hit, show cached data immediately (loading=False) but do NOT set got_status=True, so fresh fetch still proceeds via datalink or LXMF path and overwrites stale data.

When deduplicating config models, use re-export pattern in the service file: 'from styrened.models.config import XConfig  # noqa: E402' with a 'Re-export from models for backward compatibility' comment.

IPv6 ULA mesh IP derivation: DEFAULT_SUBNET_PREFIX='fd73:7479:7265:6e65' (ASCII 'styrene' hex). Interface ID is first 8 bytes of SHA-256(identity_hash) formatted as 4×16-bit groups. Gateway peers get allowed-ips subnet_prefix::/64; direct peers get /128.
mesh_vpn.py subnet prefix extraction pattern: use ':'.join(ip.split(':')[:4]) NOT ip.rsplit(':', 4)[0] — the rsplit approach breaks on compressed IPv6 notation.

Use `rich.cells.cell_len()` (not `wcwidth.wcswidth()` or `len()`) for visible character width in Textual/Rich contexts — it matches the rendering engine's behavior for East Asian Width, emoji, and zero-width chars.

asyncio.run() (not get_event_loop().run_until_complete()) should be used in pytest unit tests for async coroutines to avoid 'no current event loop' RuntimeError in Python 3.14.

public-hub deploy-roll recipe: just deploy (build+push) then kubectl rollout restart + rollout status --timeout=120s + kubectl exec styrened --version to confirm running version. One command to build, push, and verify the live pod.

public-hub build pattern: just deploy (or STYRENED_VERSION=X.Y.Z just deploy) — builds linux/amd64 with --no-cache, verifies styrened version in image, pushes latest+version+sha tags. just deploy-roll also does kubectl rollout restart + status check. public-hub Containerfile default STYRENED_VERSION changed to '0.0.0-MISSING' — if bypassed build pipeline bakes this sentinel, a clear failure signal. Real version always supplied via --build-arg from justfile.

public-hub build verification pattern: after podman build, run `podman run --rm --pull=never --platform {platform} {image} styrened --version` and compare against expected STYRENED_VERSION — exits 1 on mismatch. --pull=never is critical to test the LOCAL image, not pull from GHCR.

public-hub persistent config changes (banned_peers, etc.) must be committed to deploy/kubernetes/base/configmap.yaml in the public-hub repo and pushed to main — ArgoCD syncs from there and reverts kubectl patches.

ArgoCD sync can be triggered via kubectl patch on the Application object: kubectl patch application <name> -n argocd --type merge -p '{"operation":{"initiatedBy":{"username":"admin"},"sync":{"syncStrategy":{"apply":{"force":true}}}}}' — argocd CLI exec fails due to unspecified server address in-cluster.

title: TUI Chat Widget and Dashboard Deep Audit
narrative: The session was a detailed code review of a styrened TUI patch targeting chat widget improvements, clipboard handling, dashboard data display, and mesh hop tracking. The reviewer systematically traced data flows through RNS transport internals, IPC handlers, Textual widget lifecycle, and CSS layout to identify bugs. The audit found six critical issues including an incomplete NSPasteboard threading fix still present in paste paths, non-existent dict keys causing permanently blank TRAFFIC stats, a missing NodeStore method silently zeroing contact counts, incremental refresh not handling message deletion, and multiple concurrent dashboard worker races. Twelve additional warnings and omissions were documented, including no persistence for the new hops field and no tests for any new UI behaviors. The verdict was NEEDS REWORK.

title: Fixed critical IPC enum collision, audit issues, added 28 tests
narrative: The goal was to resolve a critical IPC command value collision where datalink commands (0x60-range intended) overlapped with terminal commands (0x50-range), causing Python's IntEnum to silently alias duplicates and misroute messages. The collision was fixed by relocating datalink commands to 0x60-0x64, and a regression test was added asserting all IPCMessageType values are unique. Alongside the critical fix, a full audit sweep addressed eight additional issues: DirectLinkService.stop() added to daemon shutdown, bridge variable initialized before try/except to prevent UnboundLocalError, _resolve() race condition patched with try/except, status cache bounded to 64 entries with LRU eviction, speedtest guarded with asyncio.Lock, bar chart scaling made relative, and dead variables removed. Twenty-eight new unit tests were written covering RTT-adaptive payload selection, cache TTL and eviction, service lifecycle, exploration table state, and the IPC collision regression. The release was tagged v0.13.29 and published to PyPI; a Dependabot high-severity alert on the repo remains open.

title: TUI screen stack dedup and r-key update check fix
narrative: The goal was to fix two TUI bugs: screen overlays stacking duplicates (double-ESC behavior) and the 'r' refresh key never triggering the version update check. The `action_open_*` guards used `isinstance(self.screen, T)` which only checks the top of the stack, so a new `_screen_in_stack(T)` helper was introduced to scan the full stack. `action_refresh()` was updated to also call `_check_for_updates()`, which is safe due to its `@work(exclusive=True)` decorator. Pre-existing uncommitted changes from a prior session (WireGuard handshake improvements, direct_link teardown hardening, daemon lifecycle, and 20 new mesh VPN tests) were batched into the same commit. All changes were released as v0.13.32 to both PyPI and GHCR.

title: Documented RBAC Security Migration Plan Across 6 Auth Surfaces
narrative: The goal was to map and preserve the full RBAC security migration plan for styrened, which had been worked out in-session analyzing all 6 independent authorization surfaces (RPC, LXMF, DirectLink, Terminal, Web API, and legacy config). The analysis identified that Phase 1 RBAC policy model was built but not yet wired into any enforcement point, with RPC being the most critical gap (fail-open, bypasses DirectLink hardening). Six ordered paths were defined with exact method targets, capability mappings, and risk assessments. All plan details were persisted to Graphiti memory across 6 entries so a new session can reconstruct the full dependency chain. The immediate next work is Phase 2: PATH 1 (RPCServer._is_authorized() → rbac.has_capability()) and PATH 2 (LXMFService._is_blocked() → rbac.resolve_role()) in a single session.

title: Assessed cross-enclave styrene features, wrote design doc
narrative: The goal was to identify and design nice-to-have features for styrene nodes communicating across enclave boundaries (hub-only peers without a direct RNS path). The session surveyed existing services — DirectLinkService, FileTransferService, MeshVPNService, RPC, and chat — to map what works cross-enclave versus what requires a direct RNS.Link. Six candidate features were analyzed: TURN-style link relay, hub-relayed file transfer, clipboard sharing, mutual discovery, async job queue, and port forwarding. The key decision was to prioritize the TURN-style relay first, since it would bridge two RNS.Links through the hub and unlock all DirectLink-dependent features (speedtest, real-time status, file transfer) without requiring per-feature LXMF fallback paths. The assessment was written to docs/CROSS-ENCLAVE-FEATURES.md; TURN relay design and implementation remain open.

title: Wired RBAC enforcement into RelayService with 3-tier gating
narrative: The goal was to close an RBAC enforcement gap in RelayService where relay capabilities were defined but not actually checked during relay session creation. The session added `_check_requester_rbac()` enforcing `relay.request` (PEER tier) and `relay.request_permanent` (OPERATOR tier), and `_check_target_rbac()` enforcing `relay.reject` and `relay.accept_permanent`. A key design decision was reclassifying `relay.reject` from the PEER tier to orthogonal (explicit grant only, like `vpn.handshake`), preventing all PEERs from automatically blocking relays. The daemon handler also received a defense-in-depth capability check. All 2689 tests pass and changes were pushed; two deferred items remain — relayed link_type field population and permanent reconnect logic — pending Phase 2 link bridging infrastructure.

title: v0.15.1 Adversarial Assessment: All 15 Findings Fixed
narrative: The session focused on completing a full adversarial code review of styrened v0.15.0 and applying all identified fixes. All 15 findings were resolved across 19 files—ranging from a critical hub status key mismatch and @work/run_worker double dispatch bug to omissions like missing config validation in SAVE_CORE_CONFIG and no deprecation warning on the ipc_bridge shim. The suite now passes 2739 tests with 5 skipped. The session ended by writing a structured memory summary of all fixes, architectural decisions, and the one known-acceptable async race condition, then compacting the context at this stable checkpoint.

title: Styrene TUI UX Framework Finalized and Stored
narrative: The session goal was to resolve all open UX questions for the Styrene TUI specification. All 5 questions were answered and committed to the design tree: TUIMode enum (OPERATOR/FLEET/KIOSK/FIELD/HEADLESS) was chosen over a bool flag, landing screens differ by mode (LocalDashboard vs full Dashboard), and progressive disclosure was adopted consistently for relay surfacing and RBAC management. The cheeky hidden toggle for switching from OPERATOR to FLEET mode was confirmed as a deliberate discovery mechanic. Session closed with memory stored; next steps are either branching child design nodes (mode-gating, screen-inventory, theming, error-handling) or writing OpenSpec scenarios for the already-decided structural refactor.
